definition_zh: 口头的；言语的；与词语有关的；逐字的；动词的
definition_en: relating to words, especially words that are spoken rather than written
core_image: 一串声音从嘴里出来，在空中排成可数的词，再落进对方的耳朵
scene: 面试结束前，主考官提醒候选人把口头承诺写成邮件，他说：Please put your verbal promise in writing.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「口头说出的、以说话方式作出的」（第 1 个义项：以口头表达而非书面写下）；句意为主考官请候选人把口头承诺落实为书面文字。

pos.zh: 口头的；言语的；词语的；逐字的；动词的
动词性词语（如动名词、动词性名词）

derivatives.zh: 言语化；用词语表达的过程
言辞表达；拘泥字面的说法
擅长言辞的人；拘泥字面者

senses.title: Spoken rather than written
senses.titleCN: 口头说出的，而非写下的
senses.definition: expressed in speech rather than in writing
senses.definitionCN: 以口头说出而不是以书面形式表达的
senses.example: She gave a verbal warning instead of a written one.
senses.exampleCN: 她做了口头警告，而没有发出书面警告。
senses.why: The root means 'word', and when a word is contrasted with a written document, the channel that remains is the voice.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根意为「词」；当它与书面文件相对时，剩下的渠道就是说话的声音。

senses.title: Relating to words or language
senses.definition: concerned with words and with the ability to use them
senses.definitionCN: 与词语以及运用词语的能力有关的
senses.example: Verbal ability predicts later reading success.
senses.exampleCN: 言语能力可以预测日后的阅读表现。
senses.why: The adjective was formed from the Latin noun for 'word', so its broadest job is simply to label anything that has to do with words.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由表示「词」的拉丁名词构成，因此最宽的用法就是给一切与词语有关的事物贴标签。

senses.title: Word-for-word and literal
senses.definition: following the exact words of an original rather than its overall meaning
senses.definitionCN: 照着原文的每一个词，而不是照着整体意思
senses.example: A verbal translation often misses the tone of the original.
senses.exampleCN: 逐字翻译常常丢掉原文的语气。
senses.why: If each word is handled separately, the translation becomes a row of separate words rather than one living sentence.
senses.whyCN: 若把每个词单独处理，译文就成了一排孤立的词，而不是一句活的话。

senses.title: Relating to a verb in grammar
senses.definition: relating to a verb or to a form built from a verb
senses.definitionCN: 与动词有关，或与由动词构成的形式有关
senses.example: The verbal ending changes with tense and person.
senses.exampleCN: 动词词尾随时态与人称变化。
senses.why: Latin used the same noun for 'word' and for 'verb', because the verb is the word that carries the action of a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语用同一个名词既指「词」也指「动词」，因为动词是承载句子动作的那个词。

senses.title: Using too many words
senses.definition: using more words than are needed to make a point
senses.definitionCN: 表达一个意思时用了超出需要的词
senses.example: His verbal style buried the main point under qualifications.
senses.exampleCN: 他冗长的说话方式把重点埋在一堆限定语下面。
senses.why: A person who piles up words is still working with words, but the abundance itself becomes the noticeable quality.
senses.whyCN: 堆词的人仍然在处理词语，只是词语的数量本身成了最显眼的特点。

senses.title: Words without matching action
senses.titleCN: 只有言辞而没有行动的
senses.definition: expressed in words but not supported by real action
senses.definitionCN: 只用言辞表达，却没有实际行动支撑
senses.example: The agreement was merely verbal and was never carried out.
senses.exampleCN: 那项约定只是口头上的，从未落实。
senses.why: When words are set against deeds, calling something verbal is a way of saying that only the talking half exists.
senses.whyCN: 当词语与行动相对时，说某事只是口头上的，就等于说只有说话那一半存在。

senses.title: Oral in a legal sense
senses.titleCN: 法律意义上的口头形式
senses.definition: made by speech rather than set down in a written instrument
senses.definitionCN: 以说话方式作出，而不是写在正式文书里
senses.example: A verbal contract can still bind the parties in some cases.
senses.exampleCN: 在某些情形下，口头合同仍能约束双方。
senses.why: Law separates a spoken declaration from a signed paper, and the word marks the side that leaves no written record.
senses.whyCN: 法律把口头声明与签字文件分开，这个词标记的正是没有留下书面记录的那一边。

senses.title: Carried by words, not by gestures
senses.titleCN: 以词语而非手势传递的
senses.definition: communicated through words rather than through bodily signals
senses.definitionCN: 通过词语而不是通过身体信号传递的
senses.example: The verbal message was clear, but the gestures softened it.
senses.exampleCN: 言语信息很清楚，但手势让它变得柔和。
senses.why: Communication research splits a message into the word channel and the body channel, and this sense names the word channel.
senses.whyCN: 交流研究把一次信息分成词语渠道与身体渠道，这个义项命名的正是词语渠道。

intro.en: Verbal comes through Middle French from Late Latin verbalis 'of words', built on Latin verbum 'word'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: verbal 经中古法语来自晚期拉丁语 verbalis「词的」，由拉丁语 verbum「词」加形容词后缀构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Verbum meant 'word' and was also the grammar term for 'verb'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link often suggested to an Indo-European root for speaking is a reconstruction, not a proven derivation.
items.cn: verbum 意为「词」，在语法中也指「动词」。其更深来源未得到证明；常有人把它系于某个表示「说话」的印欧词根，那只是重构形式，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The adjective verbalis 'relating to words' was formed from verbum and passed into learned usage.
items.cn: 形容词 verbalis「与词有关的」由 verbum 构成，并进入学术用语。

items.en: Middle French verbal carried the adjective into English in the late fourteenth century, at first in the broad sense 'of words'.
items.cn: 中古法语 verbal 在十四世纪末把这个形容词带入英语，最初用于「与词有关的」这一宽泛意义。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word was regularly opposed to written, naming what is said aloud instead of what is set down on paper.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词已常与「书面的」相对，指口头说出而非写在纸上的内容。

items.en: The grammatical sense 'of a verb' appears in the seventeenth century, and the noun for a verb-derived form developed later.
items.cn: 「与动词有关的」这一语法义在十七世纪出现，指动词性形式的名词义随后发展出来。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first date of the spoken sense is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of verbum remains unsettled, so any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：口头义的确切首见年代没有定论，verbum 在拉丁语之前的来源也仍未确定，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to verbal but follow different roots or different prefixes; group two holds near neighbours in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音接近、但词根或前缀不同的词；第二组是语义相近的词。

entries.definition: Built on the same Latin word for 'word', but it means in exactly the same words, word for word.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁语表示「词」的词，但意思是「逐字地、一字不差地」。

entries.definition: From a Latin adjective meaning 'full of words'; it describes speech or writing that uses far too many words.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示「充满词」的拉丁形容词，形容说话或写作用了过多词语。

entries.definition: It looks like a relative of the word root, but it comes from a Latin word for a home-born slave, later 'native'; it names the everyday language of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 外形像同族词，其实来自拉丁语指「家中出生的奴仆」、后转指「本地的」一词；它指一个地方日常使用的语言。

entries.definition: It descends from the same word stock through French and means an excess of words, often empty or official wording.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语同出这一词群，意思是词语过量，常指空洞或官样文字。

entries.definition: The standard adjective for what is spoken rather than written; it comes from a different Latin root meaning 'mouth'.
entries.definitionCN: 指口头而非书面的标准形容词；它来自另一个意为「嘴」的拉丁词根。

entries.definition: The ordinary English participle for language produced by voice; it is plainer than verbal and lacks the grammatical senses.
entries.definitionCN: 指用嗓音说出的语言的普通英语分词，比 verbal 朴素，也没有那些语法义。

entries.definition: Relating to language as a system; verbal can focus narrowly on individual words.
entries.definitionCN: 指与作为系统的语言有关；verbal 可以只聚焦于一个个词。

entries.definition: A plain adjective for writing or speech that uses too many words, close to the fifth sense of verbal.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话或写作词句过多的朴素形容词，接近 verbal 的第 5 个义项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real contrasts and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的对比与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'word', so verbal is the adjective for anything word-shaped.
normal.cn: 词根意为「词」，因此这个词就是给一切「词形状」的事物作形容词。

normal.en: The same root yields the adverb meaning word for word and the adjective meaning full of words.
normal.cn: 同一词根还构成表示「逐字地」的副词与表示「满口是词」的形容词。

normal.en: Contrast pair: a verbal promise is spoken, while a written promise is on paper.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：口头的承诺用嘴说，书面的承诺落在纸上。

normal.en: Grammar note: a verbal noun is a noun built from a verb, such as a gerund.
normal.cn: 语法提示：动词性名词是由动词构成的名词，如动名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the spoken sense: verbal agreement, verbal abuse, verbal skills.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出「口头」义：口头协议、言语辱骂、语言能力。

abstract.en: Picture words as small stones a speaker hands over one by one.
abstract.cn: 把词语想成说话人一颗颗递过去的小石子。

abstract.en: Picture a signed page and a spoken sentence placed on two sides of a scale.
abstract.cn: 想象一页签好的纸和一句说出的话被放在天平两端。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence made only of separate bricks, with no mortar between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话只用一块块独立的砖垒成，砖与砖之间没有灰浆。

examples.en: The manager gave only a verbal warning, so nothing appeared in the file.
examples.cn: 经理只做了口头警告，因此档案里没有留下任何记录。

examples.en: Her verbal skills made her a strong debater in seminars.
examples.cn: 她的言语能力使她在研讨会上成为强有力的辩手。

examples.en: A verbal translation of the poem lost its rhythm completely.
examples.cn: 这首诗的逐字翻译完全丢掉了节奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「我播」：我播出去的是嘴上说的话 → 口头的、词语的

root: 拉丁语 verbum「词、动词」加关系形容词后缀构成晚期拉丁语 verbalis；verbum 更深来源不确定，把它系于某个表示「说话」的印欧词根仅为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all start from one idea, the word as a unit, and then divide by channel: spoken, written, grammatical, literal, excessive, unsupported by action, legal and bodily.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个起点出发，即「词」这个单位，然后按渠道分叉：口说、书写、语法、逐字、冗长、无行动支撑、法律形式与身体信号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoken word leaving the mouth as a small, countable object.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个说出的词像可数的小物件一样离开嘴巴。

branches.en: SPOKEN CHANNEL: both the everyday warning and the legal declaration exist only in voice.
branches.cn: 口头渠道：日常警告与法律声明都只存在于声音里。

branches.en: WORD CARRIER: words themselves carry the message, whether against gestures or as a general ability.
branches.cn: 词语载体：无论与手势相对，还是作为一般能力，承载信息的都是词语本身。

branches.en: ONE WORD AT A TIME: literal translation treats each word as a separate unit.
branches.cn: 逐词处理：逐字翻译把每个词当作独立单位。

branches.en: VERB AND VERBOSITY: the same root names the action word and the habit of piling words up.
branches.cn: 动词与冗词：同一词根既命名动作词，也命名堆词的毛病。

branches.en: WORD WITHOUT DEED: the promise exists in speech but never becomes an act.
branches.cn: 有言无行：承诺只存在于言语中，从未变成行动。

intro.en: Verbal is built from a Latin root and a Latin adjectival suffix, and the same pieces recur across a small but active word family.
intro.cn: verbal 由一个拉丁词根与一个拉丁形容词后缀构成，同样的部件反复出现在一个小而活跃的词族里。

latinIntro.en: Latin verbum 'word' supplies verbal, verbatim, verbose, proverb and verb; the suffix -alis marks the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「词」的词根衍生出表示「言语的」「逐字的」「啰嗦的」「谚语」「动词」的一组词；形容词后缀标记关系。

items.meaning: word; also the grammar term for verb
items.example: The root names the smallest unit of speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名言语的最小单位。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示关系的形容词。

items.example: Verbal ability is tested in the first section.
items.exampleCN: 言语能力在第一部分接受测试。

items.example: She agreed verbally but never signed.
items.exampleCN: 她口头同意了，却始终没有签字。

items.example: He verbalized the feeling he had hidden for years.
items.exampleCN: 他把藏了多年的感受说了出来。

items.meaning: the act of putting something into words
items.meaningCN: 把某事变成词语的行为
items.example: Her verbalization of the plan made it easier to follow.
items.exampleCN: 她把计划说出来，使人更容易跟上。

items.example: He repeated the message verbatim.
items.exampleCN: 他一字不差地复述了那条信息。

items.example: The verbose report hid its conclusion.
items.exampleCN: 这份啰嗦的报告把结论藏了起来。

items.meaning: a saying passed down in fixed words
items.meaningCN: 以固定词句传下来的谚语
items.example: The old proverb still fits the case.
items.exampleCN: 那句老谚语仍适用于这件事。

latinEntries.structure: verbosus, verbosa, verbosum (adj., first and second declension)

derivatives.meaning: the act of expressing in words
a habit of relying on words

definition_zh: 非言语的；不用词语的；与身势、表情等有关的
definition_en: not involving words, especially when meaning is carried by the body, face or voice
core_image: 两个人闭着嘴，只靠眼神、手势和彼此的距离完成一次完整的交流
scene: 实验室里，研究者关掉录音设备，只记录受试者的手势与眼神，他解释道：We coded every nonverbal signal in the room.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「不使用词语、靠身体信号传递信息的」（第 1 个义项：不以语言为媒介的交流）；句意为研究者把房间里每一个非言语信号都编码记录。

pos.zh: 非言语的；不用词语的；身体信号传达的

senses.title: Not using words at all
senses.definition: communicated or carried out without any words
senses.definitionCN: 不借助任何词语而传达或完成的
senses.example: A nod is a fully nonverbal greeting.
senses.exampleCN: 点头是一种完全非言语的问候。
senses.why: The negative prefix removes the word channel and leaves every other channel available.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀去掉的正是词语渠道，留下其他所有渠道。

senses.title: Carried by body language
senses.definition: expressed through posture, hand movement, eye contact or physical distance
senses.definitionCN: 通过姿势、手部动作、眼神接触或身体距离表达的
senses.example: Her nonverbal cues revealed that she was nervous.
senses.exampleCN: 她的非言语线索暴露出她很紧张。
senses.why: The body is the next most obvious transmitter once the mouth stops providing words.
senses.whyCN: 嘴巴不再提供词语之后，身体就是最明显的下一个传递者。

senses.title: Carried by tone of voice
senses.titleCN: 由语调与嗓音特征承载的
senses.definition: conveyed by pitch, pace, loudness or voice quality rather than by word choice
senses.definitionCN: 通过音高、语速、音量或音色而不是通过选词传达的
senses.example: A nonverbal rise in pitch signaled doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 音高的非言语上扬透出了怀疑。
senses.why: A voice can carry meaning in its music as well as in its words, and this sense isolates the music.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音既能在词语里携带意义，也能在「音乐」里携带意义，这个义项分离出来的就是那层音乐。

senses.title: Measured without language
senses.definition: tested or assessed through shapes, patterns or actions instead of words
senses.definitionCN: 通过图形、图案或动作而非词语来测试或评估的
senses.example: The test uses shapes to measure nonverbal reasoning.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测试用图形来测量非言语推理。
senses.why: Psychology needed a label for abilities that can be shown without asking the subject to speak or read.
senses.whyCN: 心理学需要一个标签，指称那些不必让受试者说话或阅读就能显示出来的能力。

senses.title: Not speaking, as a clinical state
senses.titleCN: 临床意义上的不言语状态
senses.definition: remaining silent or unable to speak, often as a symptom or a temporary state
senses.definitionCN: 保持沉默或无法说话，常作为症状或暂时状态
senses.example: The child remained nonverbal for several months after the shock.
senses.exampleCN: 受惊吓后，那个孩子有几个月一直不说话。
senses.why: In clinical use the absence of speech is itself the fact being described, so the word moves from channel to condition.
senses.whyCN: 在临床用法里，说话的缺席本身就是被描述的事实，因此这个词从渠道转到了状态。

senses.title: Not functioning as a verb
senses.definition: in grammar, not having the form or function of a verb
senses.definitionCN: 在语法上不具备动词形式或功能的
senses.example: A nonverbal predicate carries no tense marking.
senses.exampleCN: 非动词性谓语不携带时态标记。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the same negative label to separate verb-like elements from everything else in a clause.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借用了同一个否定标签，把类似动词的成分与从句中其余成分分开。

senses.title: Implicit relational message
senses.definition: the part of a message that signals status, emotion or attitude without stating it in words
senses.definitionCN: 信息中不直接用词语说出、却显示地位、情绪或态度的部分
senses.example: Nonverbal messages carry most of the emotional content in a meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会议中大部分情绪内容由非言语信息承载。
senses.why: Communication research found that relationships are negotiated by glances and spacing as much as by sentences.
senses.whyCN: 交流研究发现，关系的协商既靠句子，也同样靠眼神与距离。

senses.title: Carried by images or sound
senses.titleCN: 由图像或声音而非词语承载的
senses.definition: communicated through pictures, music or sound effects rather than spoken or written language
senses.definitionCN: 通过画面、音乐或音效而不是口头或书面语言传达的
senses.example: The film's nonverbal storytelling relies on music and faces.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的非言语叙事依靠音乐与面孔。
senses.why: Media extends the word beyond the body: any channel that bypasses language can be called nonverbal.
senses.whyCN: 媒介把这个词扩展到身体之外：任何绕过语言的渠道都可以称为非言语的。

intro.en: Nonverbal is a modern English compound of the Latin negative prefix non- and the adjective verbal, which descends from Latin verbum 'word'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nonverbal 是近代英语合成词，由拉丁语否定前缀「不」与形容词 verbal 结合而成，后者源自拉丁语 verbum「词」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Non- was a negative particle in Latin and became a productive prefix meaning 'not' in English compounds.
items.cn: 拉丁语中有一个否定小品词，进入英语后成为能产的否定前缀，意为「不」。

items.en: Verbum 'word' produced the adjective verbalis, and English verbal came through French. The deeper origin of verbum is unsettled.
items.cn: verbum「词」构成形容词 verbalis，英语的 verbal 经法语而来。verbum 的更深来源尚无定论。

items.en: The compound nonverbal is recorded from the nineteenth century, often hyphenated at first, and it spread as a plain opposite of verbal.
items.cn: nonverbal 这一合成词从十九世纪起见于记录，早期常带连字符，后来作为 verbal 的朴素反义词扩散开来。

items.en: In the mid-twentieth century the word became standard in psychology and communication research, where nonverbal behavior was measured and coded.
items.cn: 到二十世纪中叶，这个词在心理学与交流研究中成为标准用语，非言语行为被测量与编码。

items.en: Clinical writing also uses the word for a patient who does not speak, which is a distinct sense rather than a reference to gestures.
items.cn: 临床文献也用这个词指不说话的患者，这是一个独立义项，而不是指手势。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first written citation of the compound is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of verbum remains a matter of reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个合成词的最早书证没有定论，verbum 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike negatives and near neighbours that are often swapped for this word; group two holds words with a similar communicative function.
note.cn: 第一组是容易被替换成这个词的外形相近否定词与近邻；第二组是交际功能相近的词。

entries.definition: It denies the voice rather than words: a nonvocal signal may still use written words, while nonverbal excludes words entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 它否定的是嗓音而不是词语：非嗓音信号仍可能用书面词语，而非言语则完全排除词语。

entries.definition: It means outside language as a system; nonverbal is narrower and usually points to a specific bodily or tonal channel.
entries.definitionCN: 指在语言系统之外；nonverbal 更窄，通常指向某个具体的身体或语调渠道。

entries.definition: It describes a person who does not speak, close to the clinical sense of nonverbal but without the communication-research meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容不说话的人，接近 nonverbal 的临床义，但不含交流研究的那层意思。

entries.definition: It means understood without being stated; its root is Latin tacere 'to be silent', so it is not a morphological relative.
entries.definitionCN: 意思是未经说出就被理解的；其词根是拉丁语 tacere「沉默」，因此并非构词上的同族词。

entries.definition: It describes the absence of sound, not the absence of words; a silent room may contain a written note.
entries.definitionCN: 形容没有声音，而不是没有词语；安静的房间里也可能有一张写好的便条。

entries.definition: A close synonym for the first sense, but it is literary and rarely used for technical research.
entries.definitionCN: 第 1 个义项的近义词，但偏文学化，很少用于技术研究。

entries.definition: It names one channel only, hand and body movement, while nonverbal can include tone, spacing and images.
entries.definitionCN: 只命名手势与身体动作这一种渠道，而 nonverbal 还可包括语调、距离与图像。

entries.definition: It describes meaning that is implied rather than declared; nonverbal describes the channel that carries it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容意义被暗示而非明说；nonverbal 描述的是承载它的渠道。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the negative prefix, the real channels and the real research terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：否定前缀、真实渠道与真实研究术语。

normal.en: The prefix means 'not', so the word literally says 'not verbal'.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「不」，所以这个词字面上就是「非言语的」。

normal.en: Four common channels: face, hands, posture and tone of voice.
normal.cn: 四个常见渠道：脸、手、姿势与语调。

normal.en: Research pair: verbal communication is counted in words, nonverbal communication in cues.
normal.cn: 研究中的配对：言语交流按词计数，非言语交流按线索计数。

normal.en: Clinical use: a patient who does not speak is described as nonverbal.
normal.cn: 临床用法：不说话的患者被描述为非言语状态。

normal.en: Testing use: a shapes-and-patterns task measures nonverbal reasoning.
normal.cn: 测试用法：图形与图案任务测量非言语推理。

abstract.en: Picture two people across a room agreeing with a single nod.
abstract.cn: 想象房间两端的两个人只用一个点头就达成一致。

abstract.en: Picture a pause that says more than the sentence before it.
abstract.cn: 想象一段停顿，比它前面那句话说得更多。

abstract.en: Picture a traffic officer whose arms direct cars without a single word.
abstract.cn: 想象一位交通协管员一句话不说，只用手臂指挥车辆。

examples.en: Teachers read nonverbal cues long before students raise a hand.
examples.cn: 老师早在学生举手之前就能读到非言语线索。

examples.en: The study found that nonverbal signals shaped trust more than words did.
examples.cn: 研究发现，非言语信号对信任的影响超过词语。

examples.en: A nonverbal reasoning task asks the solver to complete a pattern.
examples.cn: 非言语推理任务要求解题者补全一个图案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「非」加「言语的」——不用词语的 → 非言语的

root: 拉丁语否定前缀「不」加由 verbum「词」派生的 verbal；由英语在近代合成，并非古拉丁语既有词。verbum 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses remove words one channel at a time: the body, the voice, the test, silence, grammar, relational signals and finally images and sound.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项一次去掉一个渠道里的词语：身体、嗓音、测试、沉默、语法、关系信号，最后是图像与声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: meaning passes between two people while their mouths stay closed.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人闭着嘴，意义仍在彼此之间传递。

branches.en: NO WORDS AT ALL: the general exclusion of language and the clinical state of not speaking both remove the word channel completely.
branches.cn: 彻底无词：一般性地排除语言，与临床上的不说话状态，都把词语渠道完全移除。

branches.en: BODY AND RELATION: posture and spacing carry status and feeling that the sentence never states.
branches.cn: 身体与关系：姿势与距离承载句子从未说出的地位与情绪。

branches.en: VOICE MUSIC: pitch and pace carry meaning without a single new word.
branches.cn: 嗓音的音乐：音高与语速不添一个新词也能携带意义。

branches.en: TEST WITHOUT LANGUAGE: shapes and patterns measure ability while speech is kept out of the room.
branches.cn: 不用语言的测试：图形与图案测量能力，而说话被排除在外。

branches.en: OTHER SYSTEMS: grammar excludes verb function, and media exclude spoken language altogether.
branches.cn: 其他系统：语法排除动词功能，媒介则完全排除口头语言。

intro.en: Nonverbal is transparent: a negative prefix plus an adjective of words, so each part can be read on its own.
intro.cn: nonverbal 的构词很透明：一个否定前缀加一个表示词语的形容词，每一部分都能单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin non- 'not' and verbum 'word' are the two sources; English supplies the compound pattern and the modern technical senses.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的否定成分与表示「词」的词根是两个来源；英语提供合成模式与近代技术义。

items.example: The prefix turns a positive label into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把肯定标签变成其反面。

items.example: The root names the unit that the prefix removes.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名被前缀去掉的那个单位。

items.example: The suffix builds the adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示关系的形容词。

items.example: Nonverbal cues filled the silent interview.
items.exampleCN: 非言语线索充满了那场安静的面试。

items.example: The child asked for help nonverbally.
items.exampleCN: 那个孩子用非言语方式求助。

items.example: Nonverbal communication dominates first impressions.
items.exampleCN: 非言语交流主导第一印象。

items.example: A raised eyebrow is a reliable nonverbal cue.
items.exampleCN: 扬眉是一个可靠的非言语线索。

items.meaning: problem solving with patterns rather than words
items.meaningCN: 用图案而非词语解决问题
items.example: The entrance exam includes a nonverbal reasoning section.
items.exampleCN: 入学考试包含非言语推理部分。

definition_zh: 表达；表情；词语；表达方式；数学式；基因表达
definition_en: the act of showing thoughts or feelings, or the look on a face that shows them
core_image: 心里的东西被一股力量压出来，落在脸上、纸上或公式里
scene: 她听到消息后没有说话，脸上的神情却先变了，同事低声说：Her expression changed before she found the words.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「脸上显示情绪的神情」（第 2 个义项：面部神情）；句意为她还没找到话说，神情就先变了。

pos.zh: 表达；表情；词语；表达方式；数学式；基因表达

derivatives.zh: 表现主义者；表现主义的

senses.title: The act of showing thoughts or feelings
senses.titleCN: 把想法或情感表达出来的行为
senses.definition: the act of making thoughts, feelings or ideas known
senses.definitionCN: 把想法、情感或观点让人知道的行为
senses.example: Freedom of expression is protected by law.
senses.exampleCN: 表达自由受法律保护。
senses.why: The core image is pressing something inward out into the open, and the first sense is simply that outward movement.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把里面的东西压到外面来，第 1 个义项就是这一向外的动作本身。

senses.title: The look on a face
senses.definition: the appearance of a person's face that shows a feeling or state of mind
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的脸部外观所显示的情绪或心理状态
senses.example: His expression softened when he heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息，他的神情柔和下来。
senses.why: The face is the most visible surface where inner feeling is pressed into public view.
senses.whyCN: 脸是内心情感被压到公众视野里最显眼的表面。

senses.title: A word or phrase
senses.definition: a particular word, phrase or way of saying something
senses.definitionCN: 某个特定的词、短语或说法
senses.example: A local expression puzzled the translator.
senses.exampleCN: 一个当地说法让译者困惑。
senses.why: A fixed group of words is a small package into which a meaning has already been pressed.
senses.whyCN: 一组固定的词就像一个小包裹，意义早已被压进其中。

senses.title: Vivid delivery in speech or music
senses.titleCN: 说话或演奏时的表现力
senses.definition: the quality of conveying feeling through voice, phrasing or performance
senses.definitionCN: 通过嗓音、措辞或表演传达情感的特质
senses.example: She read the poem with great expression.
senses.exampleCN: 她极富表现力地朗读了这首诗。
senses.why: Once the outward push is done with skill, the delivery itself becomes noticeable and can be praised.
senses.whyCN: 当向外的推送带有技巧时，表达方式本身就会变得显眼并值得称赞。

senses.title: A mathematical expression
senses.definition: a combination of numbers, symbols and operations that stands for a value
senses.definitionCN: 由数字、符号与运算组成、代表某个值的组合
senses.example: Simplify the expression before substituting values.
senses.exampleCN: 先化简表达式，再代入数值。
senses.why: Mathematics writes a value as a visible string of symbols, pressing an abstract quantity into a readable form.
senses.whyCN: 数学把一个值写成可见的符号串，把抽象量压成可读的形式。

senses.title: Gene expression in biology
senses.definition: the process by which information in a gene is turned into a working product
senses.definitionCN: 基因中的信息被转成可用产物的过程
senses.example: The gene's expression rises under heat stress.
senses.exampleCN: 在热应激下，这个基因的表达增强。
senses.why: A gene carries hidden instructions, and expression is the moment those instructions are pushed out into the cell.
senses.whyCN: 基因携带隐藏的指令，表达就是这些指令被推到细胞里发挥作用的时刻。

senses.title: Pressing out juice or oil
senses.definition: the physical act of squeezing liquid out of fruit, seeds or peel
senses.definitionCN: 从果实、种子或果皮中挤出液体的物理动作
senses.example: Cold expression of the peel releases the essential oil.
senses.exampleCN: 冷榨果皮能释放出精油。
senses.why: This is the oldest concrete sense: the word's root literally means to press out, and liquids are pressed from plants.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的具体义：词根字面就是「压出来」，而液体正是从植物中被压出的。

senses.title: A manifestation or sign
senses.titleCN: 某种态度或品质的显现
senses.definition: an act or thing that shows a quality, attitude or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 显示某种品质、态度或情感的行为或事物
senses.example: The grant is an expression of confidence in the team.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔资助是对该团队信心的体现。
senses.why: The abstract sense generalizes the push: an inner attitude becomes visible through an outer act.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把「推送」一般化：内在态度通过外在行为变得可见。

intro.en: Expression comes through Old French from Latin expressio, a noun of action from exprimere 'to press out', built on ex- 'out' and premere 'to press'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: expression 经古法语来自拉丁语 expressio，这是动词 exprimere「压出」的行为名词，由拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀与 premere「压」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press'. Its deeper origin is not established, and the Indo-European root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: premere 意为「压」。其更深来源未得到证明，有人为它提出的印欧词根只是重构形式。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus premere produced exprimere 'to press out, squeeze out'; it also developed the sense 'to represent or portray'.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 premere 构成 exprimere「压出、挤出」；它还发展出「表现、描绘」的意义。

items.en: The action noun expressio named both a physical pressing out and a representation in words or art.
items.cn: 行为名词 expressio 既指物理上的压出，也指用词语或艺术的表现。

items.en: Old French expression entered English in the fourteenth century, first as the act of expressing and as an utterance.
items.cn: 古法语 expression 在十四世纪进入英语，最初指表达的行为与说出的话。

items.en: The facial sense took shape in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, while algebra adopted the word for a symbolic string and biology adopted it for gene activity in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 面部义在十七至十八世纪成形；代数学采用这个词指符号串，生物学则在二十世纪用它指基因活动。

items.en: Source uncertain: the date of the facial sense is not exact, and the pre-Latin origin of premere remains unsettled, so every proposed root form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：面部义的确切年代不确定，premere 在拉丁语之前的来源也仍未确定，因此提出的各种词根形式都属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built with the same pressing root but different prefixes; group two holds near neighbours in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「压」这一词根、但前缀不同的词；第二组是语义相近的词。

entries.definition: Built with 'in' rather than 'out': something presses into the mind and leaves an impression, not an outward expression.
entries.definitionCN: 用的是「向内」而非「向外」的前缀：某物压进心里留下印象，而不是向外的表达。

entries.definition: The prefix means 'together': it names pressing something into a smaller space, with no idea of showing meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀意为「共同」：指把某物压进更小的空间，与显示意义无关。

entries.definition: The prefix means 'under': it names holding something down or stopping it, often feelings or information.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀意为「在下」：指把某物压住或制止，常指情感或信息。

entries.definition: It looks as if it should belong to the pressing family, but its root means 'to appease or atone', not 'to press'.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像属于「压」这个词族，其实词根意为「安抚、赎罪」，并非「压」。

entries.definition: A plain word for the appearance of a face; expression adds the idea that the look reveals inner feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 指脸部外观的朴素词；expression 多了「神情显示内心情感」这一层。

entries.definition: A group of words forming a unit; expression can also mean a fixed saying, but it is broader and more idiomatic.
entries.definitionCN: 构成一个单位的词组；expression 也可指固定说法，但范围更宽、更习语化。

entries.definition: A technical term for a unit of speech; expression points more to the meaning being conveyed than to the sound produced.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个言语单位的技术术语；expression 更指向被传达的意义，而不是发出的声音。

entries.definition: A formal word for something that makes an inner quality visible, close to the eighth sense of expression.
entries.definitionCN: 指使内在品质变得可见的正式用词，接近 expression 的第 8 个义项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the pressing root, the prefix contrasts and the real technical uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「压」的词根、前缀对比与真实的技术用法。

normal.en: The root means 'press', so expression is a pressing outward of what was inside.
normal.cn: 词根意为「压」，因此这个词就是把里面的东西向外压出来。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: outward pressing gives expression, inward pressing gives impression.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：向外压得到「表达」，向内压得到「印象」。

normal.en: Face use: the same word names the look that shows feeling.
normal.cn: 面部用法：同一个词也命名显示情感的神情。

normal.en: Technical spread: algebra uses it for a symbolic string, biology for gene activity.
normal.cn: 技术延伸：代数学用它指符号串，生物学用它指基因活动。

normal.en: Everyday phrase: freedom of expression names the right to make ideas public.
normal.cn: 日常搭配：表达自由指把想法公开的权利。

abstract.en: Picture a hand squeezing a fruit until the juice lands in a glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手挤压果子，汁水落进杯子里。

abstract.en: Picture an inner feeling rising to the surface of a face like water to a well.
abstract.cn: 想象内心的情感升到脸的表面，像水升到井口。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence folded into a small box that can be handed to someone.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话被折进一个小盒子，可以递给别人。

examples.en: The court treated the letter as an expression of intent.
examples.cn: 法院把这封信视为意向的表达。

examples.en: Her expression did not match the cheerful words she used.
examples.cn: 她的神情与她使用的欢快词语并不一致。

examples.en: The software evaluates each expression before running the program.
examples.cn: 软件在运行程序前先求值每一个表达式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「向外」加「压」——把心里的东西压出来 → 表达、表情

root: 拉丁语 exprimere「压出」= 表示「向外」的前缀 + premere「压」，其行为名词为 expressio；premere 更深来源不确定，相关印欧词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one outward push: the act itself, the face that shows it, the phrase that packages it, the delivery, the formula, the gene, the pressed juice and the visible sign.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次向外的推送展开：行为本身、显现在脸上、被包进词语、表现方式、公式、基因、榨出的汁液以及可见的迹象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something inside is pressed outward and becomes visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：里面的东西被向外压出，变得可见。

branches.en: OUTWARD ACT: making an inner state public and letting it appear as a sign are the same push seen at two levels.
branches.cn: 向外的行为：把内在状态公开，与让它显现为迹象，是同一个推送在两个层面上的样子。

branches.en: FACE: the most visible surface on which feeling is pressed into view.
branches.cn: 脸：情感被压到视野里最显眼的表面。

branches.en: PACKAGED WORDS: a fixed phrase is a small box that already holds a meaning.
branches.cn: 被包好的词语：一个固定短语就是一只已经装着意义的小盒子。

branches.en: FORCE AND DELIVERY: the pressure that squeezes oil also shapes the skilled delivery of a line.
branches.cn: 力量与表现：挤压油液的压力，也塑造一句台词的熟练表达。

branches.en: SYMBOLIC AND BIOLOGICAL EXPRESSION: a formula makes a value readable, and a gene makes its instructions active.
branches.cn: 符号与生物表达：公式让数值可读，基因让指令发挥作用。

intro.en: Expression is made of a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a noun suffix, and the same parts build a whole family of show-and-press words.
intro.cn: expression 由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根与一个名词后缀构成，同样的部件构成了一整族表示「压出与表现」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere 'to press' and ex- 'out' produce exprimere and its noun expressio; English adds the suffixes that build the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「压」的词根与表示「向外」的前缀构成 exprimere 及其名词 expressio；英语再加上构成词族的后缀。

items.example: The prefix directs the action away from the inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作引向外部。

items.example: The root supplies the physical force in the image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供意象中的物理力量。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a name for its action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成其行为的名词。

items.example: The expression of grief took the form of silence.
items.exampleCN: 悲伤的表达采取了沉默的形式。

items.meaning: to press out; to say or show
items.example: He expressed his thanks in a short letter.
items.exampleCN: 他用一封短信表达了感谢。

items.example: Her expressive reading held the room.
items.exampleCN: 她富有表现力的朗读抓住了全场。

items.example: His expressionless face gave nothing away.
items.exampleCN: 他面无表情，没有泄露任何信息。

items.meaning: an art movement that distorts form to show feeling
items.meaningCN: 为表现情感而扭曲形式的艺术运动
items.example: Expressionism used violent colour to show inner states.
items.exampleCN: 表现主义用强烈的色彩显示内心状态。

items.example: The expressionist painted faces as blocks of colour.
items.exampleCN: 这位表现主义画家把脸画成色块。

definition_zh: 表达；表示；榨出；特快的；快递；明确的
definition_en: to say or show what you think or feel, or to press liquid out of something
core_image: 手一压，汁水从果子里出来，话从心里出来，两件事是同一个动作
scene: 早餐店里，店主把刚榨好的橙汁递给客人，说：We express the oranges fresh every morning.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「榨出、压出汁液」（第 3 个义项：用压力把汁液挤出）；句意为这家店每天早上现榨橙子。

pos.zh: 表达；表示；榨出；压出
特快的；快递的；明确的
快车；快递服务

senses.title: Say what one thinks or feels
senses.titleCN: 说出自己的想法或感受
senses.definition: to put thoughts or feelings into words
senses.definitionCN: 把想法或感受用词语说出来
senses.example: He expressed his doubts politely but clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 他有礼而清楚地表达了自己的疑虑。
senses.why: The oldest image is pressing something out, and a thought pressed out through the mouth becomes speech.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是把东西压出来，而想法从嘴里被压出就成了言语。

senses.title: Show feeling through art or action
senses.titleCN: 通过艺术或行为表现情感
senses.definition: to show a feeling or idea through a work, gesture or act rather than a statement
senses.definitionCN: 通过作品、姿态或行为而不是陈述来显示情感或观点
senses.example: The mural expresses the community's grief.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅壁画表达了社区的悲伤。
senses.why: The channel need not be words; anything that lets an inner state come out can carry the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 渠道不必是词语；任何能让内在状态出来的东西都能承载同一个动词。

senses.title: Press juice or oil out
senses.definition: to squeeze liquid out of fruit, seeds or peel by pressure
senses.definitionCN: 用压力从果实、种子或果皮中挤出液体
senses.example: The press expresses oil from the seeds.
senses.exampleCN: 压榨机从种子里榨出油。
senses.why: This is the literal root meaning, still alive in food processing and perfumery.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根的字面意义，在食品加工与香料制作中仍然活着。

senses.title: A fast train
senses.definition: a train that makes few stops and travels quickly
senses.definitionCN: 停站少、运行速度快的列车
senses.example: They caught the night express to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搭上了开往海岸的夜间特快。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century railways borrowed the word to mean a service that presses straight through without delays.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的铁路借用这个词，指一路直推、不作耽搁的服务。

senses.title: Fast delivery service
senses.definition: a service that sends letters or parcels quickly and directly
senses.definitionCN: 快速直接地寄送信件或包裹的服务
senses.example: The package went by express and arrived next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹走快递，第二天早上就到了。
senses.why: The same idea of direct speed moved from trains to mail and parcels.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「直达速度」从列车移到了邮件与包裹。

senses.title: Clearly stated and deliberate
senses.titleCN: 明确说出的；特意如此的
senses.definition: stated openly and with a clear purpose, rather than implied
senses.definitionCN: 公开说明且目的清楚，而非暗示的
senses.example: She came with the express purpose of resigning.
senses.exampleCN: 她来的明确目的就是辞职。
senses.why: Something expressly set out is pressed into clear view, so the adjective came to mean explicit.
senses.whyCN: 被明确摆出来的东西是被压进清晰视野的，因此这个形容词引申为「明确的」。

senses.title: Represent by symbols
senses.definition: to represent a value, relation or idea in symbols or a formula
senses.definitionCN: 用符号或公式表示一个值、关系或观点
senses.example: Express the ratio as a fraction in lowest terms.
senses.exampleCN: 把这个比表示成最简分数。
senses.why: Mathematics presses an abstract relation into visible symbols, continuing the same outward movement.
senses.whyCN: 数学把抽象关系压进可见符号，延续同一个向外的动作。

senses.title: Cause a gene to produce a product
senses.definition: in biology, to make the information in a gene produce a working molecule
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，使基因中的信息产生可用的分子
senses.example: These cells express the protein at high levels.
senses.exampleCN: 这些细胞高水平地表达这种蛋白质。
senses.why: A gene's instructions are pressed out into the cell as a product, which is why the same verb serves biology.
senses.whyCN: 基因的指令被压出到细胞里成为产物，因此同一个动词也服务于生物学。

intro.en: Express comes through Old French from Latin exprimere 'to press out, represent', built on ex- 'out' and premere 'to press'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: express 经古法语来自拉丁语 exprimere「压出、表现」，由拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀与 premere「压」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Premere 'to press' is the physical core. Its deeper origin is not established, and the root form often proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: premere「压」是物理核心。其更深来源未得到证明，常为它提出的词根形式属于重构。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus premere gave exprimere 'to squeeze out'; the verb then acquired the mental sense 'to represent, portray, utter'.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 premere 得到 exprimere「挤出」；这个动词随后获得「表现、描绘、说出」的心理意义。

items.en: Old French espresser and expresser carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century with both the physical and the representational senses.
items.cn: 古法语 espresser 与 expresser 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语，同时带有物理义与表现义。

items.en: From the seventeenth century a special messenger or dispatch was called an express; railways extended the label to fast trains in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，专门的信使或急件被称为 express；铁路在十九世纪把这个标签扩展到快车。

items.en: The adjective meaning 'clearly stated' developed in the sixteenth century from the idea of something expressly set out.
items.cn: 表示「明确说出」的形容词义在十六世纪发展出来，来自「被特意摆出来」的想法。

items.en: Source uncertain: exact dates of the railway and mail senses vary by region, and the pre-Latin origin of premere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：铁路义与邮件义的确切年代因地区而异，premere 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same or neighbouring roots; group two holds near synonyms for the core act of saying or showing.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词根或邻近词根的外形相近词；第二组是「说」与「显示」这一核心动作的近义词。

entries.definition: Italian borrowed the same Latin verb for coffee pressed out under steam, so the coffee and the English verb share a root.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利语借用了同一个拉丁动词，指用蒸汽压出的咖啡，因此这种咖啡与英语动词同根。

entries.definition: With 'in' rather than 'out': to press a mark or feeling into someone's mind rather than to bring something out.
entries.definitionCN: 用的是「向内」而非「向外」的前缀：把印记或感受压进某人心里，而不是把东西带出来。

entries.definition: It looks like a sibling, but its root means 'to drive', not 'to press'; it means to force someone or something out.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像同族词，其实词根意为「驱赶」而非「压」；意思是把某人或某物赶出去。

entries.definition: It shares the 'out' prefix but its root means 'to draw or pull'; extraction pulls something out rather than pressing it.
entries.definitionCN: 同样带「向外」前缀，但词根意为「拉、抽」；提取是拉出某物，而不是压出。

entries.definition: To carry an idea across to someone; it stresses successful transfer, while express stresses the outward act.
entries.definitionCN: 把想法传递给别人；强调成功送达，而 express 强调向外的动作。

entries.definition: To say something clearly and formally; express is broader and can cover art, gestures and formulas.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而正式地说出；express 更宽，可涵盖艺术、姿态与公式。

entries.definition: A formal verb for producing sounds or words; it has no physical squeezing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指发出声音或词语的正式动词；没有物理上的挤压义。

entries.definition: To express an idea clearly and in an organized way; it adds the idea of clear structure.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而有条理地表达想法；多出「结构清晰」这一层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the pressing image, the prefix contrast, the transport sense and the family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：压出意象、前缀对比、交通义与同族词。

normal.en: The root means 'press out': juice is expressed from fruit, words from a mind.
normal.cn: 词根意为「压出」：从果子里压出汁，从心里压出话。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: outward pressing is express, inward pressing is impress.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：向外压是「表达」，向内压是「给人印象」。

normal.en: Transport pair: an express train and express mail both move directly and quickly.
normal.cn: 交通配对：特快列车与快递都直达而迅速。

normal.en: The adjective with purpose means explicit, as in an express purpose.
normal.cn: 与「目的」一词连用的形容词义表示「明确的」，如明确目的。

normal.en: The family runs express, expression, expressive and expressly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括动词、名词、形容词与副词四种形式。

abstract.en: Picture an orange and a sentence both being squeezed by the same hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只橙子和一句话被同一只手挤压。

abstract.en: Picture a train that never stops until it reaches the coast.
abstract.cn: 想象一列火车一路不停，直到抵达海岸。

abstract.en: Picture a thought packed into a parcel and sent overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个想法被装进包裹，连夜寄出。

examples.en: She expressed her thanks with a small hand-written note.
examples.cn: 她用一张手写的小纸条表达了感谢。

examples.en: The factory expresses oil from locally grown seeds.
examples.cn: 这家工厂用当地种植的种子榨油。

examples.en: The express leaves the city at six and reaches the border by noon.
examples.cn: 特快列车六点离城，中午前到达边境。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「向外压」——把话压出来是说，把汁压出来是榨 → 表达、榨出

root: 拉丁语 exprimere「压出」= 表示「向外」的前缀 + premere「压」；premere 更深来源不确定，相关词根形式为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pressure: words out of a mind, feeling out through art, juice out of fruit, speed out of a schedule, clarity out of a statement, symbols out of a relation and a product out of a gene.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一股压力展开：从心里压出话语、通过艺术压出情感、从果子压出汁液、从时刻表压出速度、从陈述压出明确、从关系压出符号、从基因压出产物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand presses, and what was inside comes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：手一压，里面的东西就出来了。

branches.en: SAY AND SHOW: words and art are two outlets for the same inner pressure.
branches.cn: 说与显：词语与艺术是同一股内在压力的两个出口。

branches.en: LIQUID OUT: the literal squeeze that keeps the root meaning alive.
branches.cn: 汁液出来：字面上的挤压，让词根意义继续活着。

branches.en: DIRECT SPEED: a train and a parcel service both press straight through without delay.
branches.cn: 直达速度：列车与包裹服务都一路直推、不作耽搁。

branches.en: PRESSED INTO CLARITY: something expressly set out cannot be mistaken for an implication.
branches.cn: 压成清晰：特意摆出来的东西不会被误当成暗示。

branches.en: SYMBOL AND CELL: a formula and a gene both make an inner relation or instruction visible and active.
branches.cn: 符号与细胞：公式与基因都让内在关系或指令变得可见并发挥作用。

intro.en: Express is a Latin verb of pressing, and its parts also build nouns, adjectives and adverbs for showing and squeezing.
intro.cn: express 是一个表示「压」的拉丁动词，其部件还构成表示「表现」与「挤压」的名词、形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex- 'out' and premere 'to press' form exprimere; the noun expressio and the adjective expressus extend the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀与 premere「压」构成 exprimere；名词 expressio 与形容词 expressus 延续同一词族。

items.example: The prefix sends the action outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作送向外面。

items.example: The root names the force behind the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名动作背后的力量。

items.meaning: to press out; to say or show
items.example: The press expresses oil from the seeds.
items.exampleCN: 压榨机从种子里榨出油。

items.example: Her expression showed relief.
items.exampleCN: 她的神情显出宽慰。

items.example: The letter was warm and expressive.
items.exampleCN: 这封信温暖而富有表现力。

items.example: The rules expressly forbid the practice.
items.exampleCN: 规则明确禁止这种做法。

items.structure: Italian espresso, from the same Latin verb
items.example: The barista pulled a short espresso.
items.exampleCN: 咖啡师压出一小杯浓缩咖啡。

items.meaning: to press a mark or feeling in
items.example: The speech impressed the audience.
items.exampleCN: 这场演讲给听众留下了深刻印象。

definition_zh: 富于表现力的；表情丰富的；意味深长的
definition_en: showing feelings or meaning clearly and strongly
core_image: 一张脸或一段旋律把情绪推到观看者眼前，遮都遮不住
scene: 朗读课上，老师让学生用不同的语调读同一句话，提醒道：Try an expressive reading, not a flat one.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「富有表现力、能清楚传达情绪的」（第 1 个义项：把情感或意义有力地传达出来）；句意为老师让学生读得有表现力，而不是平铺直叙。

pos.zh: 富于表现力的；表情丰富的；意味深长的

senses.title: Clearly conveying feeling or meaning
senses.titleCN: 清楚传达情感或意义的
senses.definition: communicating feeling or meaning in a strong and clear way
senses.definitionCN: 以强烈而清楚的方式传达情感或意义
senses.example: She gave an expressive performance of the song.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这首歌唱得极富表现力。
senses.why: The suffix means 'having the quality of', and the root action is pressing out, so the word describes something that lets feeling come out strongly.
senses.whyCN: 后缀意为「具有……性质的」，词根动作是「压出」，因此这个词形容能把情感强烈释放出来的事物。

senses.title: A face or eyes that show emotion
senses.titleCN: 脸部或眼睛显露情绪的
senses.definition: showing emotion openly through facial features or the eyes
senses.definitionCN: 通过面部特征或眼神公开显示情感
senses.example: His expressive eyes gave him away before he spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 他还没开口，会说话的眼睛就出卖了他。
senses.why: The face is the most direct surface for expression, so an expressive face is one where the inner state is easy to read.
senses.whyCN: 脸是表达最直接的表面，因此「表情丰富的脸」就是内心状态容易被读出的脸。

senses.title: Emotionally powerful art or music
senses.titleCN: 情感力量强烈的艺术或音乐
senses.definition: full of emotional force in performance, sound or visual form
senses.definitionCN: 在表演、声音或视觉形式中充满情感力量
senses.example: The cello line is quietly expressive.
senses.exampleCN: 大提琴的旋律线含蓄而富有表现力。
senses.why: Art can press feeling out through shape and sound, so the same adjective applies to a painting or a phrase of music.
senses.whyCN: 艺术能通过形状与声音把情感压出，因此同一个形容词也适用于绘画或一段音乐。

senses.title: Precise and vivid language
senses.definition: using words in a way that carries a vivid impression
senses.definitionCN: 用词能带来鲜明印象的
senses.example: An expressive phrase can carry a whole scene.
senses.exampleCN: 一个生动的短语就能承载整个场景。
senses.why: When words are chosen so that meaning comes out sharply, the language itself is called expressive.
senses.whyCN: 当词语被选到让意义鲜明地出来时，语言本身就被称为富有表现力。

senses.title: Attitude meaning in linguistics
senses.titleCN: 语言学中表达态度的意义
senses.definition: in linguistics, carrying the speaker's emotion or attitude rather than plain reference
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，携带说话人的情感或态度，而非单纯指称
senses.example: Expressive meaning includes surprise, affection and irritation.
senses.exampleCN: 表达性意义包括惊讶、喜爱与恼怒。
senses.why: Language has a layer that shows how the speaker feels about what is said, and that layer is called expressive.
senses.whyCN: 语言有一层显示说话人对所述内容感受的成分，这一层被称为表达性的。

senses.title: Meaningful gesture or movement
senses.titleCN: 意味深长的手势或动作
senses.definition: conveying meaning through bodily movement rather than words
senses.definitionCN: 通过身体动作而不是词语传达意义
senses.example: Her expressive hands shaped the idea in the air.
senses.exampleCN: 她富有表现力的双手在空中把那个想法塑了出来。
senses.why: Hands can press a meaning into space, which is why a gesture can be described with the same word as a face.
senses.whyCN: 双手能把意义压进空间里，因此一个手势也能用与脸相同的词来形容。

senses.title: Full of character in style or design
senses.titleCN: 风格或设计上个性鲜明的
senses.definition: having a strong and distinctive character in form or style
senses.definitionCN: 在形式或风格上有强烈而独特个性的
senses.example: The building's expressive roof divides opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑个性鲜明的屋顶让人评价两极。
senses.why: Design can also push an attitude outward, so a bold shape may be called expressive even without words.
senses.whyCN: 设计也能把一种态度向外推出，因此大胆的形状即使没有词语也可称为有表现力。

senses.title: Serving as a sign of something
senses.definition: acting as a visible sign of a quality, feeling or fact
senses.definitionCN: 作为某种品质、情感或事实的可见标志
senses.example: The vote was expressive of public anger.
senses.exampleCN: 那次投票体现了公众的愤怒。
senses.why: The construction with 'of' turns the adjective into a pointer: the visible thing shows what lies behind it.
senses.whyCN: 与表示「关于」的介词连用时，这个形容词变成指针：可见之物显示出它背后的东西。

intro.en: Expressive joins express, from Latin exprimere 'to press out', with the Latin suffix -ivus, which marks a tendency or quality. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: expressive 由 express（源自拉丁语 exprimere「压出」）加拉丁语形容词后缀构成，该后缀标记倾向或性质。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus premere 'to press' gave exprimere, whose senses included squeezing out and representing in words or art.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 premere「压」构成 exprimere，其意义包括挤出，以及用词语或艺术表现。

items.en: The suffix -ivus formed adjectives of tendency or quality, as in words describing what something tends to do or is full of.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词后缀构成表示倾向或性质的形容词，用来描述某物倾向于做什么或充满什么。

items.en: English expressive appears in the sixteenth century as the adjective of expression, first in the sense of serving to express.
items.cn: 英语 expressive 在十六世纪出现，作为 expression 的形容词，最初表示「用于表达的」。

items.en: By the seventeenth century it had acquired the stronger sense 'full of expression, vivid, showing feeling clearly'.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，它获得了更强的意义「充满表现力、生动、清楚显示情感」。

items.en: Later applications extend to art, music, design and linguistics, where the word labels emotional or attitudinal meaning.
items.cn: 后来的用法扩展到艺术、音乐、设计与语言学，在这些领域标记情感或态度意义。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of premere remains unsettled, so proposed root forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：确切的最早书证没有定论，premere 在拉丁语之前的来源也仍未确定，因此提出的词根形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds morphological neighbours that differ by prefix or suffix; group two holds near synonyms for vivid showing.
note.cn: 第一组是靠前缀或后缀区分开的构词近邻；第二组是表示「鲜明显示」的近义词。

entries.definition: With 'in' rather than 'out': it describes something that presses a strong effect into the mind, not something that shows feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 用的是「向内」而非「向外」的前缀：形容某物把强烈效果压进心里，而不是显示情感。

entries.definition: The suffix means 'can be': it says that something is capable of being put into words, not that it is vivid.
entries.definitionCN: 后缀意为「能够被」：表示某事可以被用词语说出来，而不是生动。

entries.definition: It describes an art style that gives an impression of a scene; the inward prefix marks it as a cousin rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 形容一种给人场景印象的艺术风格；向内的前缀表明它是同族而非同义词。

entries.definition: It is the direct opposite: a face or performance that shows no feeling at all.
entries.definitionCN: 它是直接的反面：完全不显示情感的脸或表演。

entries.definition: It stresses fluent, persuasive speech; expressive can apply to a face, a sound or a design.
entries.definitionCN: 强调流利而有说服力的言辞；expressive 可用于脸、声音或设计。

entries.definition: It describes something that produces a strong mental image; expressive focuses on the feeling being pushed outward.
entries.definitionCN: 形容能产生强烈心理画面的东西；expressive 聚焦于被向外推出的情感。

entries.definition: It means causing emotion in the audience; expressive means full of emotion that is being shown.
entries.definitionCN: 意为在观众身上激起情感；expressive 意为充满并显示情感。

entries.definition: It stresses the successful passing of information; expressive stresses the force and feeling of the display.
entries.definitionCN: 强调信息成功传递；expressive 强调展示的力量与情感。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the suffix of quality, the outward root and the real domains of use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示性质的后缀、向外的词根与真实的使用领域。

normal.en: The suffix means 'having the quality of', so expressive means having the quality of pressing feeling out.
normal.cn: 后缀意为「具有……性质」，因此这个词意为具有把情感压出来的性质。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: outward pressing is expressive, inward pressing is impressive.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：向外压是「有表现力」，向内压是「给人深刻印象」。

normal.en: Three domains: an expressive face, an expressive line of music, an expressive phrase.
normal.cn: 三个领域：表情丰富的脸、富有表现力的乐句、生动的短语。

normal.en: The opposite is built with the suffix meaning 'without'.
normal.cn: 反义词由表示「没有」的后缀构成。

normal.en: Linguistics uses the word for the layer of language that shows the speaker's attitude.
normal.cn: 语言学用这个词指语言中显示说话人态度的层次。

abstract.en: Picture a face that tells the whole story before a single word is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸在一个字说出之前就讲完了整个故事。

abstract.en: Picture a melody that makes the room go quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象一段旋律让整个房间安静下来。

abstract.en: Picture a gesture so clear that it needs no translation.
abstract.cn: 想象一个清楚到不需要翻译的手势。

examples.en: The actor's expressive face carried the silent scene.
examples.cn: 演员表情丰富的脸撑起了那场无声的戏。

examples.en: Her letter was expressive of gratitude rather than apology.
examples.cn: 她的信体现的是感激，而不是歉意。

examples.en: The dialect uses expressive particles to show surprise.
examples.cn: 这种方言用表达性小品词来表示惊讶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「有表现力的」——把心里的情绪压到脸上、声音里 → 表情丰富的

root: 拉丁语 exprimere「压出」的过去分词词干加拉丁形容词后缀；前缀表「向外」，词根 premere 表「压」。premere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one quality to different surfaces: performance, face, art, language, attitude, gesture, design and visible sign.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一种性质用到不同表面：表演、脸、艺术、语言、态度、手势、设计与可见标志。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feeling is pushed out so strongly that others can read it at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：情感被强烈地推出来，别人一眼就能读到。

branches.en: GENERAL QUALITY: the broad claim that something conveys feeling or meaning clearly.
branches.cn: 一般性质：某物能清楚传达情感或意义的宽泛判断。

branches.en: FACE: the surface where emotion is easiest to read.
branches.cn: 脸：情绪最容易被读出的表面。

branches.en: ART AND GESTURE: sound and bodily movement both shape feeling in visible or audible form.
branches.cn: 艺术与手势：声音与身体动作都把情感塑成可见或可听的形式。

branches.en: LANGUAGE LAYERS: vivid wording and the speaker's attitude both add feeling to plain reference.
branches.cn: 语言层次：生动的措辞与说话人的态度都给单纯指称添上情感。

branches.en: DESIGN AND SIGN: a bold form and a visible indication both point beyond themselves.
branches.cn: 设计与标志：大胆的形式与可见的指示都指向自身之外。

intro.en: Expressive is the adjective of quality built on the pressing verb, and its suffix can be compared with the suffixes of its neighbours.
intro.cn: expressive 是在表示「压」的动词上构成的性质形容词，它的后缀可以与邻近词的后缀相比较。

latinIntro.en: Latin exprimere supplies the root; -ivus supplies the sense 'tending to or full of', and English adds -ly and -ness for the adverb and noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exprimere 提供词根；形容词后缀提供「倾向于或充满」的意义，英语再加副词后缀与名词后缀构成新词。

items.example: The face can express what speech hides.
items.exampleCN: 脸能表达言语所隐藏的东西。

items.meaning: tending to; having the quality of
items.example: The suffix turns an action into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成性质。

items.example: Her expressive voice held the audience.
items.exampleCN: 她富有表现力的嗓音抓住了听众。

items.meaning: in a way that shows feeling
items.example: He read the line expressively.
items.exampleCN: 他富有表现力地读了那一行。

items.example: The dancer's expressiveness silenced the hall.
items.exampleCN: 舞者的表现力让全场安静下来。

items.meaning: the act or result of showing
items.example: The painting is an expression of grief.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画是悲伤的表达。

items.example: His inexpressive reply concealed his anger.
items.exampleCN: 他毫无表情的回应掩盖了怒气。

items.example: The scale of the bridge is impressive.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥的规模令人印象深刻。

items.meaning: able to be put into words
items.example: The feeling was real but hardly expressible.
items.exampleCN: 那种感受很真实，却几乎无法用语言表达。

definition_zh: 手势；姿态；表示心意的举动；做手势
definition_en: a movement of the hand or body that expresses an idea or feeling, or an action meant to show an attitude
core_image: 手在半空画出一个形状，把看不见的意思递到对方眼前
scene: 谈判陷入僵局时，对方递来一杯水，这个小动作让气氛缓和下来，他后来说：The offer was a gesture of goodwill.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「表示善意的一个举动」（第 2 个义项：用以表达态度或心意的行为）；句意为递水这个举动是一种善意表示。

pos.zh: 手势；姿态；表示心意的举动；象征性动作
做手势；用动作表示

senses.title: A hand or body movement with meaning
senses.titleCN: 带有意义的手部或身体动作
senses.definition: a movement of the hand, arm or body used to express an idea or direct attention
senses.definitionCN: 用手、臂或身体的动作来表达想法或引导注意
senses.example: She made a gesture to indicate the exit.
senses.exampleCN: 她做了个手势，指向出口。
senses.why: The core of the word is a carried movement: the body performs something that carries meaning to another person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是一个被「带过去」的动作：身体做出某件事，把意义带到别人那里。

senses.title: An action that shows an attitude
senses.definition: an action performed to show a feeling, intention or attitude rather than to achieve a practical result
senses.definitionCN: 为显示情感、意图或态度而不是为取得实际结果所做的行为
senses.example: Returning the gift was a gesture of refusal.
senses.exampleCN: 退回礼物是一种拒绝的表示。
senses.why: The word moves from the hand to the whole act: what is carried across is now an attitude, not a shape in the air.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从手扩展到整个行为：被带过去的不再是空中的形状，而是一种态度。

senses.title: A mere show with no real effect
senses.titleCN: 只具形式而无实际作用的姿态
senses.definition: an act that looks meaningful but changes nothing in practice
senses.definitionCN: 看起来有意义、实际却不改变任何事情的行为
senses.example: The apology was a gesture, not a remedy.
senses.exampleCN: 那次道歉只是姿态，并不是补救。
senses.why: When the outward movement carries no real weight, the word can name an empty form.
senses.whyCN: 当向外的动作没有真正的分量时，这个词就可以指空有形式的举动。

senses.title: A movement in dance or visual art
senses.titleCN: 舞蹈或视觉艺术中的动作
senses.definition: a single movement or shape used as a unit of expression in dance, painting or sculpture
senses.definitionCN: 舞蹈、绘画或雕塑中作为一个表达单位的单个动作或形状
senses.example: The choreographer built the piece from small gestures.
senses.exampleCN: 编舞者用一个个小动作搭建起整支作品。
senses.why: Art isolates the bodily movement itself and treats it as a complete expressive unit.
senses.whyCN: 艺术把身体动作本身分离出来，把它当作一个完整的表现单位。

senses.title: To move the body in order to express
senses.definition: to make a movement of the hand or body in order to show or point something out
senses.definitionCN: 用手或身体的动作来显示或指出某事物
senses.example: He gestured toward the door and waited.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝门口做了个手势，然后等着。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb without changing its core: the body still carries the message.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词，核心没有变：仍然是身体在承载信息。

senses.title: Co-speech movement in linguistics
senses.titleCN: 语言学中与言语同步的动作
senses.definition: in linguistics, a hand movement that accompanies speech and helps organize its meaning
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，伴随言语出现并帮助组织意义的手部动作
senses.example: Gesture and speech are processed together by the listener.
senses.exampleCN: 听者会把手势与言语放在一起处理。
senses.why: Research found that hand movements are not decoration but a parallel channel that runs alongside speech.
senses.whyCN: 研究发现手部动作不是装饰，而是与言语并行的另一条渠道。

senses.title: Stage action in theatre
senses.definition: a physical action or piece of business used by an actor on stage
senses.definitionCN: 演员在舞台上使用的身体动作或小动作
senses.example: The actor's gesture filled the silence.
senses.exampleCN: 演员的动作填满了那段沉默。
senses.why: On stage the body must carry meaning when dialogue stops, so the movement becomes a unit of performance.
senses.whyCN: 在舞台上，对话停止时身体必须承载意义，因此动作成为表演的单位。

senses.title: A touchscreen movement
senses.definition: a movement of the fingers on a screen that gives a device a command
senses.definitionCN: 手指在屏幕上移动，向设备发出指令
senses.example: A swipe is a common gesture on a touchscreen.
senses.exampleCN: 滑动是触屏上常见的手势。
senses.why: The old bodily movement acquired a new machine reader: the screen now interprets the shape of the hand.
senses.whyCN: 古老的身体动作有了新的机器读者：屏幕现在会解读手的形状。

intro.en: Gesture comes through Medieval Latin gestura and French from Latin gestus 'bearing, gesture', formed from gerere 'to carry, perform'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gesture 经中世纪拉丁语 gestura 与法语，来自拉丁语 gestus「姿态、手势」，后者由 gerere「携带、施行」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gerere meant 'to carry, conduct, perform'. Its deeper origin is not established, and the root often proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: gerere 意为「携带、进行、施行」。其更深来源未得到证明，常为它提出的词根属于重构形式。

items.en: The past participle gestus named a bearing or carriage of the body, and from it came the idea of a deliberate movement.
items.cn: 过去分词 gestus 指身体的姿态与举止，由它产生了「有意的动作」这一意义。

items.en: Medieval Latin gestura meant a bearing or gesture and passed into English through French in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 gestura 意为姿态或手势，在十五世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: The verb to gesture appears in the sixteenth century, formed directly from the noun.
items.cn: 动词用法在十六世纪出现，直接由名词构成。

items.en: Later centuries extended the word to symbolic public acts, stage business and, most recently, finger movements on screens.
items.cn: 后来的世纪把这个词扩展到象征性的公共举动、舞台动作，以及最近屏幕上的手指动作。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first date of the symbolic-act sense is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of gerere remains unsettled; forms offered for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：象征举动义的确切首见年代没有定论，gerere 在拉丁语之前的来源也未确定，为它给出的形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes that come from the same carrying root or from unrelated roots; group two holds near synonyms for a meaningful movement.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近、或同出「携带」词根、或完全异源的词；第二组是表示有意义动作的近义词。

entries.definition: It comes from the same root but means to make gestures in an exaggerated or excited way.
entries.definitionCN: 同出这个词根，但意思是夸张或激动地打手势。

entries.definition: It descends from a related verb meaning 'to carry', but it names the carrying of a fetus, not a movement of the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 来自一个意为「携带」的相关动词，但指携带胎儿，而不是手部动作。

entries.definition: It sounds close but comes from a Latin word for a joke or game, so it is not related in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 读音接近，但来自拉丁语指玩笑或游戏，因此并不同源。

entries.definition: A German borrowing for an organized whole; its shape resembles this word but shares no Latin root with it.
entries.definitionCN: 借自德语，指有组织的整体；外形相似，但与本词没有共同的拉丁词根。

entries.definition: A general word for anything that carries meaning, including written marks; gesture is specifically bodily.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何携带意义之物的宽泛词，包括书写符号；gesture 特指身体动作。

entries.definition: A cue sent deliberately to convey information; gesture can be unconscious and need not be addressed to anyone.
entries.definitionCN: 为传递信息而有意发出的线索；gesture 可以是无意识的，也不必指向任何人。

entries.definition: It names movement in general, without implying that the movement carries a meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指运动本身，不暗示该动作携带意义。

entries.definition: A single downward movement of the head used as a gesture of agreement or greeting.
entries.definitionCN: 头部向下的单个动作，用作同意或问候的手势。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the carrying root, the real kin and the real modern uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「携带」的词根、真实的同族词与真实的现代用法。

normal.en: The root means 'carry or perform', so a gesture is a movement that carries meaning.
normal.cn: 词根意为「携带、施行」，因此手势就是携带意义的动作。

normal.en: The same root yields the verb for exaggerated gesturing and the noun for carrying a fetus.
normal.cn: 同一词根还构成表示夸张打手势的动词与表示怀胎的名词。

normal.en: Three levels: a hand movement, a symbolic act and an empty show.
normal.cn: 三个层次：手部动作、象征举动与空有姿态。

normal.en: Stage use: when dialogue stops, the body must carry the scene.
normal.cn: 舞台用法：对话停下时，身体必须撑起场景。

normal.en: Modern use: a swipe on a screen is now called a gesture.
normal.cn: 现代用法：屏幕上的一次滑动现在也被称为手势。

abstract.en: Picture an idea too small for words being handed over by a hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一个太小而不便用言语表达的想法，被一只手递了过去。

abstract.en: Picture a gift offered across a table when words have failed.
abstract.cn: 想象言语失效时，一件礼物被从桌子对面递过来。

abstract.en: Picture a finger drawing a line on glass to make a machine answer.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在玻璃上画一道线，让机器作出回应。

examples.en: He opened the door for her, a small gesture of courtesy.
examples.cn: 他为她开门，这是一个表示礼貌的小举动。

examples.en: The teacher gestured for the class to gather round the table.
examples.cn: 老师做手势让学生们围到桌边。

examples.en: The peace talks produced gestures but no binding agreement.
examples.cn: 和谈产生了一些姿态，却没有具有约束力的协议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「杰斯特」——手上做一个漂亮动作 → 手势、姿态

root: 拉丁语 gerere「携带、施行」的过去分词 gestus「姿态、手势」，再派生中世纪拉丁语 gestura「举止、手势」；gerere 更深来源不确定，相关词根形式为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one carried movement: a meaningful hand shape, a public act, an empty form, a unit of art, the verb, co-speech movement, stage action and a screen command.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个被携带的动作展开：有意义的手形、公开举动、空洞形式、艺术单位、动词用法、伴随言语的动作、舞台动作与屏幕指令。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the body draws a shape in the air and hands its meaning to another person.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体在空中画出一个形状，把它的意义递给另一个人。

branches.en: HAND MOVEMENT: the noun and the verb both centre on a body shape that points or shows.
branches.cn: 手部动作：名词与动词都聚焦于一个用来指向或显示的身体形状。

branches.en: PUBLIC ACT: an attitude can be carried by an act, and that act can be full of meaning or empty of effect.
branches.cn: 公开举动：态度可以由行为承载，而这个行为可以有意义，也可以没有实际效果。

branches.en: ART AND STAGE: dance and theatre isolate the movement and make it a unit of expression.
branches.cn: 艺术与舞台：舞蹈与戏剧把动作分离出来，使它成为表达单位。

branches.en: CO-SPEECH: the hand runs alongside the voice and helps organize meaning.
branches.cn: 伴随言语：手与嗓音并行，帮助组织意义。

branches.en: MACHINE READER: the screen becomes a new audience for the shape of the hand.
branches.cn: 机器读者：屏幕成为手部形状的新观众。

intro.en: Gesture is a Latin noun of bearing and carrying, and its root also builds words about posture, carrying and exaggerated movement.
intro.cn: gesture 是一个表示姿态与携带的拉丁名词，其词根还构成与姿势、携带及夸张动作有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin gerere 'to carry, perform' gives gestus and gestura; English adds suffixes for the adjective, the verb of gesturing and the noun of that action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gerere「携带、施行」衍生出 gestus 与 gestura；英语再加后缀构成形容词、打手势的动词及该动作的名词。

items.example: The root names what the body does with a movement.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名身体对一个动作所做的处理。

items.example: Gestus covered the whole carriage of the body.
items.exampleCN: 这个词涵盖整个身体的举止。

items.structure: gestura, gesturae (f., first declension, Medieval Latin)
items.example: Medieval Latin gestura passed through French into English.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语中的这个词经法语进入英语。

items.example: A gesture can replace a sentence.
items.exampleCN: 一个手势可以替代一句话。

items.example: Gestural meaning depends on context.
items.exampleCN: 手势意义取决于语境。

items.example: He gesticulated while telling the story.
items.exampleCN: 他讲故事时手舞足蹈。

items.example: Her gesticulation made the point without words.
items.exampleCN: 她夸张的手势不用词语就把意思说明了。

items.meaning: the carrying of young in the body
items.example: The same carrying root also names pregnancy.
items.exampleCN: 同一个表示「携带」的词根也命名怀孕。

items.example: The story was told gesturally.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事是用手势讲述的。

definition_zh: 手势的；用手势表达的；笔触奔放的
definition_en: relating to or done with gestures
core_image: 一排手的轨迹留在空中，像写字一样留下看得见的笔画
scene: 画家不用细线勾边，而是大幅挥臂涂抹，评论家评价说：The painting is gestural rather than precise.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「笔触奔放、以身体动作留下的痕迹为特征的」（第 3 个义项：绘画中强调挥洒动作的风格）；句意为这幅画是挥洒式的，而非精细描摹。

pos.zh: 手势的；用手势表达的；笔触奔放的

senses.title: Relating to gestures
senses.definition: concerning gestures or the use of bodily movement to express meaning
senses.definitionCN: 与手势或使用身体动作表达意义有关的
senses.example: Gestural meaning depends heavily on context.
senses.exampleCN: 手势意义在很大程度上取决于语境。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun to whatever it describes, so its broadest job is 'of gestures'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词连接到被描述之物，因此最宽的用法就是「与手势有关的」。

senses.title: Communicated by gestures
senses.definition: carried by bodily movement rather than by speech
senses.definitionCN: 由身体动作而不是言语承载的
senses.example: The children developed a rich gestural system of their own.
senses.exampleCN: 这些孩子发展出了自己丰富的手势系统。
senses.why: When a message is delivered by hands instead of words, the channel itself is named by this adjective.
senses.whyCN: 当信息由手而不是词语送达时，这个形容词命名的就是该渠道本身。

senses.title: Loose, action-based brushwork
senses.titleCN: 笔触奔放、以动作留下的画风
senses.definition: in painting, marked by visible sweeping movements of the hand or arm
senses.definitionCN: 在绘画中，以手或臂明显挥扫留下的痕迹为特征
senses.example: The portrait's gestural strokes suggest motion.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像奔放的笔触暗示着运动。
senses.why: Modern painting made the painter's physical movement visible on the canvas, so the gesture became the style.
senses.whyCN: 现代绘画让画家的身体动作留在画布上可见，于是手势本身成了风格。

senses.title: Movement-based in dance
senses.definition: built from bodily movement as its main material
senses.definitionCN: 以身体动作为主要材料构建的
senses.example: The solo is purely gestural, with almost no music.
senses.exampleCN: 这段独舞纯粹以动作为本，几乎没有音乐。
senses.why: Dance strips expression down to movement, and this adjective marks that reduction.
senses.whyCN: 舞蹈把表达削减到动作本身，这个形容词标记的正是这种削减。

senses.title: Accompanying speech in linguistics
senses.definition: describing hand movements that run alongside speech and help organize it
senses.definitionCN: 描述与言语并行、帮助组织言语的手部动作
senses.example: Gestural cues help listeners resolve ambiguous sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 手势线索帮助听者消解歧义句。
senses.why: Speech is not alone; the hands add a parallel stream that researchers describe with this word.
senses.whyCN: 言语并不孤单；双手提供一条并行的流，研究者用这个词描述它。

senses.title: Controlled by hand movement
senses.definition: in computing, operated by movements of the hand or fingers instead of a mouse or keyboard
senses.definitionCN: 在计算中，用手或手指的动作而不是鼠标或键盘操作
senses.example: Gestural input replaced the mouse in the new interface.
senses.exampleCN: 在新界面里，手势输入取代了鼠标。
senses.why: Machines learned to read the hand, so the adjective moved from art and dance into interface design.
senses.whyCN: 机器学会了读手，这个形容词便从艺术与舞蹈进入界面设计。

senses.title: Physically shaping sound in music
senses.titleCN: 音乐中以身体动作塑造声音的
senses.definition: describing the conductor's or performer's use of bodily movement to shape sound
senses.definitionCN: 描述指挥或演奏者用身体动作塑造声音
senses.example: The conductor's gestural language was unusually clear.
senses.exampleCN: 这位指挥的手势语言格外清楚。
senses.why: A conductor shapes music through the air before a note is played, which is gesture used as instruction.
senses.whyCN: 指挥在音符响起之前就在空中塑造音乐，这是把动作当作指令。

senses.title: Signed rather than spoken
senses.titleCN: 以手语而非口语表达的
senses.definition: describing a language or utterance produced with the hands and body rather than the voice
senses.definitionCN: 描述用手与身体而不是嗓音产生的语言或话语
senses.example: Sign languages are fully gestural and fully grammatical.
senses.exampleCN: 手语完全是手势性的，也完全具备语法。
senses.why: A signed language is a complete language in the gestural channel, so the adjective can name its medium.
senses.whyCN: 手语是在手势渠道中完整运作的语言，因此这个形容词可以命名它的媒介。

intro.en: Gestural is an English adjective formed from gesture, which comes through Medieval Latin gestura from Latin gestus 'bearing'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gestural 是由 gesture 构成的英语形容词；gesture 经中世纪拉丁语 gestura 来自拉丁语 gestus「姿态」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gestus named the bearing or carriage of the body, from gerere 'to carry, perform'. The deeper origin of gerere is not established.
items.cn: gestus 指身体的姿态与举止，来自 gerere「携带、施行」。gerere 的更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: Gestura carried the same meaning into Medieval Latin and then into French and English.
items.cn: gestura 把同一意义带入中世纪拉丁语，再进入法语与英语。

items.en: English gesture appears in the fifteenth century as a noun for a movement or bearing.
items.cn: 英语 gesture 在十五世纪出现，指动作或举止。

items.en: Gestural is recorded in the seventeenth century, formed with the English adjective suffix -al.
items.cn: gestural 在十七世纪见于记录，由英语关系形容词后缀构成。

items.en: The art sense describing loose, action-based brushwork belongs to modern criticism and the study of painting technique.
items.cn: 描述奔放、以动作为本的笔触这一艺术义属于现代批评与绘画技法研究。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation of the adjective is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of gerere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个形容词确切的最早书证没有定论，gerere 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that look alike or share the gesture root; group two holds near neighbours describing movement-based expression.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近或同出「手势」词根的词；第二组是描述「以动作为本的表现」的近义词。

entries.definition: The noun itself names the movement; the adjective describes whatever is made of or done with such movements.
entries.definitionCN: 名词本身命名动作；这个形容词则描述由这种动作构成或完成的事物。

entries.definition: It describes a style full of exaggerated gesture, not the general quality of being gestural.
entries.definitionCN: 形容充满夸张手势的风格，而不是一般意义上的「手势性的」。

entries.definition: It sounds close in art talk but comes from a word for weaving and refers to surface texture.
entries.definitionCN: 在艺术讨论中读音接近，但来自表示「编织」的词，指表面质地。

entries.definition: A German term for an organized whole; it shares a shape with this word but no Latin origin.
entries.definitionCN: 指有组织整体的德语术语；与这个词外形相似，但不同源。

entries.definition: It means done with the hands, often physical work; gestural stresses expression rather than labour.
entries.definitionCN: 意为用手完成的，常指体力工作；gestural 强调表达而不是劳动。

entries.definition: It covers every wordless channel; gestural is narrower and names the hand-and-body channel.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖所有无词渠道；gestural 更窄，命名手与身体的渠道。

entries.definition: It describes the strength of feeling shown; gestural describes the medium through which it is shown.
entries.definitionCN: 描述所显示情感的力量；gestural 描述显示它的媒介。

entries.definition: It relates to motion itself, especially in art; gestural adds the idea of meaningful bodily action.
entries.definitionCN: 与运动本身有关，尤其在艺术中；gestural 多出「有意义的身体动作」这一层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the adjective suffix, the art sense and the modern interface sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：形容词后缀、艺术义与现代界面义。

normal.en: The noun names the movement; adding the adjective suffix makes a word for anything built from it.
normal.cn: 名词命名动作；加上形容词后缀，就得到描述由它构成之物的词。

normal.en: Art use: visible sweeping brushmarks are called gestural strokes.
normal.cn: 艺术用法：看得见的挥扫笔痕被称为挥洒式笔触。

normal.en: Dance use: a movement-only solo is a gestural piece.
normal.cn: 舞蹈用法：只靠动作的独舞是手势性作品。

normal.en: Technology use: a gestural interface reads the hand instead of a mouse.
normal.cn: 技术用法：手势界面读手，而不是读鼠标。

normal.en: Sign language is a fully gestural language, not a set of pantomime tricks.
normal.cn: 手语是完整的手势语言，不是一套哑剧把戏。

abstract.en: Picture a brush moving so fast that the movement itself stays on the canvas.
abstract.cn: 想象画笔快得让动作本身留在了画布上。

abstract.en: Picture hands shaping a sentence in the air for eyes instead of ears.
abstract.cn: 想象双手在空中为眼睛而不是耳朵塑出一句话。

abstract.en: Picture a conductor drawing a curve that becomes a phrase of music.
abstract.cn: 想象指挥画出的一道弧线变成了一段音乐。

examples.en: The museum labels the work as gestural abstraction.
examples.cn: 博物馆把这件作品标为手势性抽象画。

examples.en: Deaf communities use a fully gestural language with its own grammar.
examples.cn: 聋人群体使用一种有自身语法的完整手势语言。

examples.en: The new headset offers gestural control for simple commands.
examples.cn: 这款新头显为简单指令提供手势控制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 手势加「的」——凡是由手部动作构成的 → 手势的、挥洒式的

root: 英语 gesture 加关系形容词后缀；gesture 来自中世纪拉丁语 gestura，再上溯拉丁语 gestus「姿态」，源自动词 gerere「携带、施行」。gerere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply the same adjective to different media: gesture in general, wordless messages, paint, dance, speech, interfaces, conducting and sign language.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用到不同媒介：一般手势、无词信息、绘画、舞蹈、言语、界面、指挥与手语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visible trace of the hand left in air, paint or light.
core.cn: 核心意象：手在空中、颜料里或光线中留下的可见痕迹。

branches.en: GENERAL RELATION: the plain adjective for anything concerning gestures.
branches.cn: 一般关系：用于任何与手势有关之物的朴素形容词。

branches.en: WORDLESS LANGUAGE: a gesture system and a signed language both carry full meaning without speech.
branches.cn: 无词语言：手势系统与手语都能不用口语承载完整意义。

branches.en: PAINT: the painter's arm leaves its movement visible on the surface.
branches.cn: 绘画：画家的手臂把动作留在表面可见。

branches.en: PERFORMANCE: dance and conducting both shape expression through trained bodily movement.
branches.cn: 表演：舞蹈与指挥都通过训练有素的身体动作塑造表达。

branches.en: SPEECH AND MACHINE: hands run beside the voice and, in interfaces, replace the mouse.
branches.cn: 言语与机器：手与嗓音并行，在界面中还取代鼠标。

intro.en: Gestural is the adjective built on the gesture noun, and the family around it describes different kinds of bodily movement.
intro.cn: gestural 是在 gesture 这一名词上构成的形容词，它周围的词族描述不同类型的身体动作。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root gerere 'to carry, perform' produced gestus and gestura; English forms gesture, gestural and the verb gesticulate from the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词根 gerere「携带、施行」产生 gestus 与 gestura；英语由同一词群构成 gesture、gestural 与动词 gesticulate。

items.example: A gesture carried the message.
items.exampleCN: 一个手势承载了信息。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.meaningCN: 手势的或以手势完成的
items.example: The work is gestural from edge to edge.
items.exampleCN: 这幅作品从一边到另一边都是挥洒式的。

items.example: The scene was directed gesturally.
items.exampleCN: 这场戏是用手势语言指导的。

items.example: He gesticulated to make the point clear.
items.exampleCN: 他用力打手势把观点说明白。

items.example: Her gesticulation amused the class.
items.exampleCN: 她夸张的手势逗乐了全班。

items.example: The term is rare but follows the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: 这个术语罕见，但遵循同一构词模式。

items.meaning: a system controlled by hand movement
items.meaningCN: 用手部动作控制的系统
items.example: The game uses a gestural interface.
items.exampleCN: 这个游戏使用手势界面。

definition_zh: 面部表情；脸上显示情绪的神情
definition_en: the look on a person's face that shows emotion or intention
core_image: 一张脸像仪表盘，把内里的情绪显示在表面
scene: 演员没有台词，只靠一张脸完成整场戏，导演在排练后说：The facial expression carried the whole scene.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「脸上显示情绪的神情」（第 1 个义项：面部呈现出的情绪状态）；句意为整场戏靠面部表情撑了起来。

pos.zh: 面部表情；脸上的神情

senses.title: The look on a face that shows emotion
senses.definition: the visible state of a person's face that reveals a feeling
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的脸部所显示、透露某种情感的外观状态
senses.example: Her facial expression told us she had won.
senses.exampleCN: 她的面部表情告诉我们她赢了。
senses.why: The phrase joins the surface of the face to the outward pressing of feeling, so it names feeling made visible on the face.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把脸的表面与情感的向外压出结合起来，因此命名的是在脸上变得可见的情感。

senses.title: The act of producing such a look
senses.definition: the activity of moving the face so as to show a feeling
senses.definitionCN: 通过脸部动作来显示情感的活动
senses.example: Facial expression is studied frame by frame in the laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室逐帧研究面部表情的产生。
senses.why: The same phrase can name the activity rather than the result, as when researchers measure how a look is produced.
senses.whyCN: 同一个短语也可以命名活动而不是结果，例如研究者测量神情是如何产生的。

senses.title: A specific configuration
senses.definition: a particular arrangement of the features, such as a smile or a frown
senses.definitionCN: 五官的某种特定排列，如微笑或皱眉
senses.example: A raised eyebrow is a familiar facial expression.
senses.exampleCN: 扬眉是一种人们熟悉的面部表情。
senses.why: Once a look is repeatable, it becomes a named pattern that can be recognized across faces.
senses.whyCN: 当一种神情可以重复出现时，它就成为一个可跨面孔识别的命名模式。

senses.title: A measurable muscular pattern in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学中可测量的肌肉模式
senses.definition: in psychology, a coordinated pattern of facial muscle activity that can be coded
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中可被编码的面部肌肉协同活动模式
senses.example: Researchers coded each facial expression by action unit.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者按动作单元对每一种面部表情进行编码。
senses.why: Psychology turned the visible look into a measurable event, so the phrase names a pattern of muscle activity.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把可见的神情变成可测量的事件，因此这个短语命名的是一种肌肉活动模式。

senses.title: A controlled display in acting
senses.definition: a deliberately shaped look used by an actor to convey a character's state
senses.definitionCN: 演员为传达角色状态而有意塑造的神情
senses.example: The actor rehearsed the facial expression in a mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 演员对着镜子练习这个面部表情。
senses.why: Performance treats the look as a craft object that can be practised, held and released on cue.
senses.whyCN: 表演把神情当作可练习、可保持、可按提示释放的手艺对象。

senses.title: A nonverbal signal in communication
