senses.definition: a wordless signal that can support, qualify or contradict what is said
senses.definitionCN: 一种无词信号，可以支持、限定或反驳所说的话
senses.example: A facial expression can contradict the words being spoken.
senses.exampleCN: 面部表情可能与正在说的话相矛盾。
senses.why: In interaction the face sends a message of its own, which may agree or disagree with the voice.
senses.whyCN: 在互动中，脸发出自己的信息，可能与嗓音一致，也可能不一致。

senses.title: A clinical sign
senses.definition: in medicine, a look of the face that indicates a neurological or physical state
senses.definitionCN: 医学中指示神经或身体状态的面部外观
senses.example: A mask-like facial expression appeared early in the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病早期就出现了面具样的面部表情。
senses.why: Medicine reads the face as evidence, so a fixed or altered look becomes a sign of a condition.
senses.whyCN: 医学把脸当作证据来读，因此固定或改变的神情成为某种病状的征兆。

senses.title: A depicted look in portraiture
senses.definition: the look represented by an artist in a portrait or figure
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家在肖像或人物形象中再现的神情
senses.example: The portrait's facial expression is deliberately ambiguous.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像的面部表情被有意画得含混。
senses.why: Art represents a face rather than possessing one, so the phrase names a depicted look.
senses.whyCN: 艺术是再现一张脸而不是拥有一张脸，因此这个短语命名的是被描绘的神情。

intro.en: Facial expression joins two Latin-derived words: facial, from facies 'form, face', and expression, from exprimere 'to press out'. The compound is modern English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: facial expression 由两个源自拉丁语的词结合而成：facial 来自 facies「形状、脸」，expression 来自 exprimere「压出」。这一合成词属近代英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Facies meant 'form, appearance, face'. Its deeper origin is not established, and proposed links to a root for making or shaping are reconstructions.
items.cn: facies 意为「形状、外观、脸」。其更深来源未得到证明，把它系于某个表示「制作、塑形」的词根只是重构。

items.en: The adjective facialis 'of the face' was formed from facies and entered English through French.
items.cn: 形容词 facialis「脸的」由 facies 构成，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: Expression descends from exprimere 'to press out, represent', built on ex- 'out' and premere 'to press'.
items.cn: expression 源自 exprimere「压出、表现」，由表示「向外」的前缀与表示「压」的词根构成。

items.en: The phrase facial expression became common in the eighteenth century, when physiognomy and portraiture paid close attention to the readable face.
items.cn: facial expression 这一短语在十八世纪变得常见，当时相面术与肖像画都密切关注可读的脸。

items.en: In the twentieth century psychology and medicine turned the phrase into a technical label for measurable or diagnostic facial patterns.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，心理学与医学把这个短语变成可测量或可诊断的面部模式的技术标签。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation of the compound is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origins of facies and premere remain unsettled; proposed forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个合成词确切的最早书证没有定论，facies 与 premere 在拉丁语之前的来源也未确定，提出的形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the parts and close morphological relatives of the phrase; group two holds near synonyms for the look of a face.
note.cn: 第一组是这个短语的组成部分与构词近亲；第二组是表示脸部外观的近义词。

entries.definition: The adjective alone means 'of the face' and can describe nerves, features or treatments, not only expressions.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词单独使用时意为「脸的」，可描述神经、五官或护理，不只描述表情。

entries.definition: A medical term for the characteristic appearance of the face, often used in diagnosis; it is the Latin source of facial.
entries.definitionCN: 指面部特征性外观的医学术语，常用于诊断；它是 facial 的拉丁语来源。

entries.definition: The everyday English noun for the front of the head, which came through French from the same Latin source.
entries.definitionCN: 指头部正面的日常英语名词，经法语来自同一拉丁语来源。

entries.definition: On its own it can mean any act of showing feeling, a phrase or a mathematical formula; the compound narrows it to the face.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时可以指任何表达情感的行为、词语或数学式；合成后收窄到脸。

entries.definition: A plain word for the appearance of the face; the compound adds the idea that the look reveals feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 指脸部外观的朴素词；这个合成短语多出「神情透露情感」这一层。

entries.definition: A literary word for the face and its expression, often suggesting composure or character.
entries.definitionCN: 指脸及其表情的文学用词，常暗示镇定或品格。

entries.definition: A formal or literary word for a face, especially its appearance; it does not focus on the emotion shown.
entries.definitionCN: 指脸、尤其是其外观的正式或文学用词；不聚焦于所显示的情绪。

entries.definition: The study or appearance of facial features as signs of character; the compound is about momentary feeling, not permanent character.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或指面部特征作为性格标志；这个合成短语讲的是短暂情绪，而不是持久性格。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the face word, the expression word, the research use and the stage use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「脸」的词、「表达」的词、研究用法与舞台用法。

normal.en: The first word means 'of the face', the second means 'a showing', so the phrase is a showing on the face.
normal.cn: 第一个词意为「脸的」，第二个词意为「显示」，因此整个短语就是「脸上的显示」。

normal.en: The face has a small set of reusable patterns: smile, frown, raised brow, blank stare.
normal.cn: 脸有一套可重复使用的小模式：微笑、皱眉、扬眉、空白凝视。

normal.en: Research use: psychologists code the look muscle by muscle.
normal.cn: 研究用法：心理学家把神情一块肌肉一块肌肉地编码。

normal.en: Stage use: an actor can hold a look through a long silent shot.
normal.cn: 舞台用法：演员能在漫长的无声镜头里保持一种神情。

normal.en: Medical use: a fixed, mask-like look can be a sign of illness.
normal.cn: 医学用法：固定、面具般的神情可能是疾病的征兆。

abstract.en: Picture a face as a dashboard where each feeling lights a different lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象脸是一块仪表盘，每种情绪点亮不同的灯。

abstract.en: Picture a portrait that keeps a secret by refusing to settle into one look.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅肖像拒绝固定成一种神情，从而守住一个秘密。

abstract.en: Picture a smile that disagrees with the sentence being spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一个微笑与正在说出的句子互相矛盾。

examples.en: The interviewer noted his neutral facial expression and calm voice.
examples.cn: 面试官注意到他中性的面部表情与平静的嗓音。

examples.en: Software can now recognize a facial expression in a crowd.
examples.cn: 软件如今能在人群里识别面部表情。

examples.en: Her facial expression softened as the child ran toward her.
examples.cn: 孩子朝她跑来时，她的面部表情柔和下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「脸部的」加「表达」——脸把情绪表达出来 → 面部表情

root: facial 来自拉丁语 facies「形状、脸」的形容词 facialis；expression 来自拉丁语 exprimere「压出」。短语为近代英语合成；facies 与 premere 的更深来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the visible look to the act that produces it, then to a named pattern, a measured muscle event, a stage craft, a signal, a symptom and a painted image.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从可见的神情，走到产生它的行为，再到命名的模式、被测量的肌肉事件、舞台手艺、信号、症状与画中的形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the face as a surface where an inner state becomes visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：脸是一块让内在状态变得可见的表面。

branches.en: LOOK AND MAKING THE LOOK: the visible state and the activity that produces it are two sides of one event.
branches.cn: 神情与造出神情：可见状态与产生它的活动是同一事件的两面。

branches.en: NAMED PATTERN: a repeatable arrangement such as a smile becomes a recognizable unit.
branches.cn: 命名模式：像微笑这样可重复的排列成为一个可识别的单位。

branches.en: MEASURED AND DIAGNOSTIC: the same look can be coded as muscle activity or read as a medical sign.
branches.cn: 测量与诊断：同一神情既可被编码为肌肉活动，也可被读作医学体征。

branches.en: MADE AND DEPICTED: an actor shapes a look, and a painter represents one.
branches.cn: 塑造与描绘：演员塑造神情，画家再现神情。

branches.en: SIGNAL: the face sends a message that may support or contradict the voice.
branches.cn: 信号：脸发出的信息可以支持嗓音，也可以与之矛盾。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a face adjective and an expression noun, and both halves bring their own Latin relatives into English.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个表示「脸」的形容词与一个表示「表达」的名词构成，两半都各自带着拉丁语亲属进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin facies 'face' gives facial and facies; exprimere 'press out' gives expression and expressive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facies「脸」衍生 facial 与 facies；exprimere「压出」衍生 expression 与 expressive。

items.example: The Latin noun names the whole visible form.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词命名整个可见的形状。

items.example: The adjective entered English as facial.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词作为独立词进入英语。

items.example: The suffix marks relation to the face.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记与脸的关系。

items.example: A facial nerve controls the muscles of the look.
items.exampleCN: 面部神经控制神情所用的肌肉。

items.example: The twins are facially similar.
items.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎在面部上相似。

items.example: The expression on her face changed first.
items.exampleCN: 她脸上的表情先变了。

items.example: He has a highly expressive face.
items.exampleCN: 他有一张表情非常丰富的脸。

items.example: The software reads facial expression in real time.
items.exampleCN: 软件实时读取面部表情。

items.example: Facial recognition is a different task from expression analysis.
items.exampleCN: 人脸识别与表情分析是不同的任务。

definition_zh: 身体语言；体态语；姿势传达的信息
definition_en: the way a person's posture, movements and physical signals communicate meaning without words
core_image: 一个人站着的样子，本身就是一句不用嘴说出的句子
scene: 面试时她不停交叉双臂，面试官把这个信号记在纸上，后来解释道：Her body language suggested resistance.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「通过姿势与动作传达态度的非言语方式」（第 1 个义项：不用词语的身体信号系统）；句意为她的身体语言显得抗拒。

pos.zh: 身体语言；体态语；姿势传达的信息

senses.title: Nonverbal communication through posture and movement
senses.titleCN: 通过姿势与动作进行的非言语交流
senses.definition: the system of signals sent by posture, movement, spacing and touch rather than words
senses.definitionCN: 由姿势、动作、距离与触碰而不是词语发出的信号系统
senses.example: Body language often reveals more than words do.
senses.exampleCN: 身体语言常常比词语透露得更多。
senses.why: The compound treats the body as a language: it has signals, patterns and a reading process, though no grammar of words.
senses.whyCN: 这个合成词把身体当成一种语言：它有信号、模式与解读过程，只是没有词语语法。

senses.title: A person's current posture as an attitude signal
senses.titleCN: 某人当下的姿势所显示的态度
senses.definition: the immediate stance and movements of one person that suggest comfort, confidence or resistance
senses.definitionCN: 一个人当下的站姿与动作，暗示舒适、自信或抗拒
senses.example: His body language was open and relaxed during the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会议期间他的身体语言开放而放松。
senses.why: At this scale the phrase names one body's present state rather than a general system.
senses.whyCN: 在这个层面上，这个短语命名的是一个身体当下的状态，而不是一般系统。

senses.title: Culturally variable signals
senses.definition: bodily signals whose meaning changes from one culture or community to another
senses.definitionCN: 意义在不同文化或群体之间发生变化的身体信号
senses.example: The same body language can mean different things abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 同样的身体语言在国外可能有不同含义。
senses.why: The body is universal, but the code attached to it is learned, so the phrase can mark cultural difference.
senses.whyCN: 身体是普遍的，但附着其上的代码是习得的，因此这个短语可以标记文化差异。

senses.title: Unconscious cues in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学中无意识的线索
senses.definition: bodily signals that leak feelings without the person intending to send them
senses.definitionCN: 在本人无意发送时泄露情感的身体信号
senses.example: Researchers measured body language during the interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者在访谈期间测量身体语言。
senses.why: Psychology treats much bodily signalling as automatic, which is why it can betray what speech conceals.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把许多身体信号视为自动发生，因此它能出卖言语所隐藏的东西。

senses.title: Animal posture signals
senses.definition: the postures and movements by which an animal signals mood or intention
senses.definitionCN: 动物用来表示情绪或意图的姿势与动作
senses.example: The dog's body language warned us to stay back.
senses.exampleCN: 那只狗的身体语言警告我们退后。
senses.why: The phrase extends beyond humans because animals also read stance, tail and distance as signals.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语扩展到人类之外，因为动物也把站姿、尾巴与距离读作信号。

senses.title: A skill taught in professional settings
senses.titleCN: 职业培训中教授的技能
senses.definition: the practical ability to read and control bodily signals in sales, negotiation or leadership
senses.definitionCN: 在销售、谈判或领导中读取与控制身体信号的实用能力
senses.example: The workshop taught body language for negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 这场工作坊教授谈判中的身体语言。
senses.why: Once the signals are understood, they become a trainable skill rather than a mere fact of behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这些信号被理解，它们就成为可训练的技能，而不只是行为事实。

senses.title: Expressive physicality in performance
senses.titleCN: 表演中富有表现力的身体动作
senses.definition: the deliberate use of posture and movement by a performer to convey character or mood
senses.definitionCN: 表演者有意使用姿势与动作传达角色或情绪
senses.example: The dancer's body language filled the empty stage.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者的身体语言填满了空荡的舞台。
senses.why: Performance uses the same bodily code deliberately, turning everyday stance into expressive material.
senses.whyCN: 表演有意使用同一套身体代码，把日常站姿变成表现材料。

senses.title: Digital body language
senses.titleCN: 数字交流中的身体语言
senses.definition: the tone, timing, punctuation and emoji that stand in for bodily signals in text
senses.definitionCN: 在文字交流中替代身体信号的语气、时机、标点与表情符号
senses.example: Emoji and punctuation form a kind of digital body language.
senses.exampleCN: 表情符号与标点构成一种数字身体语言。
senses.why: When bodies are absent, writers rebuild the missing signals with marks on a screen.
senses.whyCN: 当身体不在场时，写作者用屏幕上的符号重建缺失的信号。

intro.en: Body language is an English compound of body, from Old English bodig, and language, from Latin lingua 'tongue' through Old French. The phrase is a modern coinage. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: body language 是英语合成词，由源自古英语 bodig 的 body 与经古法语来自拉丁语 lingua「舌头」的 language 组成。这个短语是近代新造。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bodig meant the physical frame of a person or animal; its further origin is obscure and not settled.
items.cn: bodig 指人或动物的身体骨架；其更早来源模糊，没有定论。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue, language'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and the forms proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: lingua 意为「舌头、语言」。其更深来源不确定，为它提出的形式属于重构。

items.en: Old French langage carried the word into English as language, first meaning the faculty of speech and then a system of signs.
items.cn: 古法语 langage 把这个词带入英语成为 language，最初指说话能力，后指符号系统。

items.en: The phrase body language is recorded in the early twentieth century and became widely popular with mid-century writing on nonverbal communication.
items.cn: body language 这一短语在二十世纪初见于记录，并随二十世纪中叶关于非言语交流的写作而广泛流行。

items.en: Later it became a practical label in sales, negotiation and leadership training, where reading stance was treated as a skill.
items.cn: 后来它成为销售、谈判与领导力培训中的实用标签，读懂姿势被视为一种技能。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation of the compound is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of lingua remains unsettled, so proposed forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个合成词确切的最早书证没有定论，lingua 在拉丁语之前的来源也未确定，提出的形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds compounds and technical terms that look close but name different things; group two holds near synonyms for wordless signalling.
note.cn: 第一组是外形接近却指不同事物的合成词与术语；第二组是表示无词信号的近义词。

entries.definition: It names the internal rhythm that regulates sleep and hunger, not a system of signals.
entries.definitionCN: 命名调节睡眠与饥饿的内部节律，而不是信号系统。

entries.definition: A political metaphor for a nation as an organized whole; the body here is figurative and not communicative.
entries.definitionCN: 把国家比作有组织的整体的政治隐喻；这里的身体是比喻性的，并不传达信息。

entries.definition: A full language with grammar and vocabulary made of hand and body signs; body language is unsystematic and not a language in that sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由手与身体符号构成、具备语法与词汇的完整语言；body language 不系统，也不是那个意义上的语言。

entries.definition: It names tone, pace and volume that accompany speech; body language excludes the voice.
entries.definitionCN: 指伴随言语的语调、语速与音量；body language 不包括嗓音。

entries.definition: The academic study of bodily movement as communication; the compound is the everyday name for the behaviour studied.
entries.definitionCN: 研究身体动作作为交流的学术领域；这个合成词是该行为的日常名称。

entries.definition: Only the arrangement of the body while standing or sitting; body language includes movement, spacing and touch as well.
entries.definitionCN: 只指站立或坐着时身体的排列；body language 还包括动作、距离与触碰。

entries.definition: The academic term for all wordless signalling, including tone and images; body language is the bodily part.
entries.definitionCN: 指所有无词信号的学术术语，包括语调与图像；body language 是其中身体的部分。

entries.definition: A person's overall manner and bearing, which may suggest character; body language focuses on signals and their reading.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的整体举止与风度，可暗示性格；body language 聚焦于信号及其解读。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two parts of the compound, the main channels and the technical contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：合成词的两个部分、主要渠道与技术对比。

normal.en: The compound says the body behaves like a language: signals, patterns, reading.
normal.cn: 这个合成词说身体像一种语言：有信号、模式与解读。

normal.en: Main channels: posture, hand movement, eye contact, spacing and touch.
normal.cn: 主要渠道：姿势、手部动作、眼神接触、距离与触碰。

normal.en: Contrast pair: body language is bodily, while paralanguage is vocal but still wordless.
normal.cn: 对比配对：body language 是身体的，而副语言是嗓音的、同样无词的。

normal.en: Professional use: sales and negotiation training treats it as a readable skill.
normal.cn: 职业用法：销售与谈判培训把它当作可解读的技能。

normal.en: Modern extension: emoji and punctuation are called digital body language.
normal.cn: 现代延伸：表情符号与标点被称为数字身体语言。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing still, yet saying a whole paragraph by stance alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人一动不动，却只靠站姿就说出一整段话。

abstract.en: Picture a dog lowering its head before any sound is made.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狗在发出任何声音之前先低下头。

abstract.en: Picture a text message whose punctuation does the work of a raised eyebrow.
abstract.cn: 想象一条短信，靠标点做出扬眉的动作。

examples.en: Her crossed arms were read as defensive body language.
examples.cn: 她交叉的双臂被读作防御性的身体语言。

examples.en: The trainer asked the class to notice body language during interviews.
examples.cn: 培训师让学员留意面试中的身体语言。

examples.en: In some cultures, the same body language is considered polite rather than rude.
examples.cn: 在某些文化里，同样的身体语言被视为礼貌而非粗鲁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「身体」加「语言」——身体不用嘴也在说话 → 身体语言

root: 英语合成词：body 源自古英语 bodig「身体」，language 经古法语来自拉丁语 lingua「舌头、语言」。短语为近代新造；两词的更深来源均有不确定处。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the general system to one person's posture, cultural codes, unconscious cues, animal signals, trained skill, stage expression and the digital substitute.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般系统，走到一个人的姿势、文化代码、无意识线索、动物信号、受训技能、舞台表达与数字替代物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a standing body that forms a sentence without opening its mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个站着的身体不张嘴就组成了一句话。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND ONE BODY: the general code and a single person's present stance are the same signals at two scales.
branches.cn: 系统与单个身体：一般代码与一个人当下的站姿，是同一套信号的两个尺度。

branches.en: CULTURE: the same stance can carry different meanings in different communities.
branches.cn: 文化：同样的站姿在不同群体中可携带不同意义。

branches.en: READING AND TRAINING: unconscious cues can be measured, and then taught as a practical skill.
branches.cn: 解读与训练：无意识线索可以被测量，然后作为实用技能被教授。

branches.en: ANIMAL: posture and distance signal mood beyond the human case.
branches.cn: 动物：姿势与距离在人类之外也传达情绪。

branches.en: STAGE AND SCREEN: performers use the code deliberately, and writers rebuild it with punctuation and emoji.
branches.cn: 舞台与屏幕：表演者有意使用这套代码，写作者则用标点与表情符号重建它。

intro.en: Body language is a two-word compound; each half has its own history, and the pair became a fixed label for wordless signalling.
intro.cn: body language 是一个两词合成短语；两半各有自己的历史，合在一起成为无词信号的固定标签。

latinIntro.en: English body comes from Old English bodig, while language comes from Latin lingua 'tongue' through Old French; the compound itself is modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 英语 body 源自古英语 bodig，而 language 经古法语来自拉丁语 lingua「舌头」；合成短语本身是近代英语。

items.example: The body carries signals before speech begins.
items.exampleCN: 身体在言语开始之前就携带信号。

items.example: The Latin noun named both the organ and the faculty.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词既指器官，也指能力。

items.example: The suffix helped form language from the French verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀帮助从法语动词构成表示「语言」的词。

items.example: The phrase borrows the word language for the body.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语把「语言」一词借给了身体。

items.example: Body language shaped the interview.
items.exampleCN: 身体语言影响了那场面试。

items.meaningCN: 作定语放在另一名词前
items.example: Body-language research grew after the war.
items.exampleCN: 身体语言研究在战后发展起来。

items.example: A tilted head is a body language cue.
items.exampleCN: 歪头是一个身体语言线索。

items.meaning: a person who reads such signals professionally
items.meaningCN: 以解读这类信号为职业的人
items.example: The body language expert warned against overreading.
items.exampleCN: 这位身体语言专家提醒不要过度解读。

definition_zh: 交谈；会话；谈话；（正式）会谈；人机对话
definition_en: an informal talk in which people exchange ideas, news or feelings
core_image: 两个人把话来回抛接，像传球一样，谁都不一直握着球
scene: 两人在厨房边洗碗边聊到深夜，第二天他回忆说：That conversation changed how I saw the problem.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「两个人之间的交谈」（第 1 个义项：面对面的口头交流）；句意为那场谈话改变了他看问题的方式。

pos.zh: 交谈；会话；谈话；正式会谈；人机对话
（较少用）与……交谈

senses.title: An informal spoken exchange
senses.definition: a talk between people in which ideas, news or feelings are exchanged informally
senses.definitionCN: 人们之间非正式交换想法、消息或情感的谈话
senses.example: We had a long conversation about her plans.
senses.exampleCN: 我们围绕她的计划聊了很久。
senses.why: The root image is a turning together: each speaker turns the talk back toward the other, so no one holds the floor for good.
senses.whyCN: 词根意象是「一起转动」：每个说话人都把话转回对方，因此没有人一直占着话语权。

senses.title: A particular instance of talking
senses.definition: one specific occasion or stretch of talking between people
senses.definitionCN: 人们之间某一个具体场合或一段具体的谈话
senses.example: I overheard an interesting conversation on the train.
senses.exampleCN: 我在火车上偶然听到一段有趣的谈话。
senses.why: An activity can also be counted as an event, so the same noun names one bounded episode.
senses.whyCN: 一种活动也可以被数成一次事件，因此同一个名词也命名一个有始有终的片段。

senses.title: Formal talks between groups
senses.definition: organized discussions between representatives of groups, states or organizations
senses.definitionCN: 团体、国家或组织代表之间有组织的讨论
senses.example: The two governments opened conversations on trade.
senses.exampleCN: 两国政府就贸易开启了会谈。
senses.why: The informal exchange can be scaled up to institutions, where the talk is planned and consequential.
senses.whyCN: 非正式交流可以放大到机构层面，在那里谈话是有计划的且有后果的。

senses.title: The social skill of talking
senses.definition: the ability to keep a light talk going and make others comfortable
senses.definitionCN: 让轻松的谈话继续、让他人感到自在的能力
senses.example: He is good at making conversation at parties.
senses.exampleCN: 他擅长在聚会上与人寒暄。
senses.why: A skill is what a person brings to the activity, so the noun can name the ability rather than the event.
senses.whyCN: 技能是个人带到活动中的东西，因此这个名词可以命名能力而不是事件。

senses.title: Spoken practice in language learning
senses.titleCN: 语言学习中的口语练习
senses.definition: a classroom activity in which learners practise speaking with each other
senses.definitionCN: 学习者在课堂上互相练习口语的活动
senses.example: The class focuses on conversation rather than grammar drills.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课侧重口语交谈，而不是语法操练。
senses.why: Teaching isolates the spoken exchange as a practice object, so the noun becomes a method label.
senses.whyCN: 教学把口头交流分离出来当作练习对象，因此这个名词成为方法标签。

senses.title: Written dialogue in a text
senses.definition: the speech of characters represented in a novel, play or script
senses.definitionCN: 小说、戏剧或剧本中再现的人物言语
senses.example: The novel's conversation scenes feel improvised.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的对话场景像是即兴的。
senses.why: Writing can imitate the turn-taking of talk, so the noun names represented speech as well as live speech.
senses.whyCN: 写作可以模仿谈话的轮流交替，因此这个名词也命名被再现的言语，而不只是现场言语。

senses.title: A human-machine exchange
senses.definition: a series of messages exchanged with a computer assistant or chatbot
senses.definitionCN: 与计算机助手或聊天机器人交换的一系列消息
senses.example: The assistant keeps track of the conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 助手会记录整段对话。
senses.why: As machines learned to take turns in talk, the word extended to a new kind of partner.
senses.whyCN: 当机器学会在谈话中轮流发言，这个词便扩展到一种新的对话伙伴。

senses.title: An ongoing public discussion
senses.definition: a society-wide debate carried on across media over time
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会通过多种媒体长期进行的辩论
senses.example: The documentary entered the national conversation on water.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片加入了全国关于水资源的公共讨论。
senses.why: Many private talks can add up to one large public exchange, so the singular noun can name a society's ongoing argument.
senses.whyCN: 许多私人谈话可以汇成一场大型公共交流，因此单数名词可以命名一个社会持续的讨论。

intro.en: Conversation comes through Old French from Latin conversatio 'familiarity, manner of living', from conversari 'to keep company', which is built on convertere 'to turn around'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: conversation 经古法语来自拉丁语 conversatio「亲近、生活方式」，后者出自 conversari「与人相处」，而这个词又由 convertere「转向」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vertere meant 'to turn'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and the root form often proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转动」。其更深来源不确定，常为它提出的词根形式属于重构。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus vertere gave convertere 'to turn around, turn about'.
items.cn: 表示「共同」的前缀加 vertere 构成 convertere「转向、回转」。

items.en: Conversari meant 'to live with, keep company, have dealings with'; the talk was part of the company, not yet the whole meaning.
items.cn: conversari 意为「与……同住、交往、打交道」；谈话只是相处的一部分，还不是全部意义。

items.en: Conversatio named familiar intercourse or a manner of life, and this is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: conversatio 指亲近的交往或生活方式，这是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French conversation entered English in the fourteenth century, and by the sixteenth century the modern sense 'talk between people' had become central.
items.cn: 古法语 conversation 在十四世纪进入英语，到十六世纪「人与人之间的谈话」这一现代义已成为核心。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact date when the sense shifted from 'living together' to 'talking' is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of vertere remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：从「共同生活」转向「谈话」的确切年代没有定论，vertere 在拉丁语之前的来源也未确定。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same turning root or from misleadingly similar roots; group two holds near synonyms for talk.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「转动」词根、或词根容易混淆的词；第二组是表示谈话的近义词。

entries.definition: It comes from the same turning verb but means a change of form, belief or use, not a talk.
entries.definitionCN: 同出表示「转动」的动词，但意思是形式、信仰或用途的改变，而不是谈话。

entries.definition: It looks like a close relative but comes from a root meaning 'to keep safe', not 'to turn'.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像近亲，其实来自表示「守住」的词根，而不是「转动」。

entries.definition: It means familiar with a subject, from the idea of having dealings with it; it does not mean talkative.
entries.definitionCN: 意为熟悉某个主题，来自「与之打交道」的想法；并不是「爱说话」的意思。

entries.definition: As a verb it means to talk, and as a noun it means the opposite statement; the shorter word has a wider logical use.
entries.definitionCN: 作动词意为交谈，作名词意为相反的命题；这个较短的词有更宽的逻辑用法。

entries.definition: It stresses exchange between two or more sides, often in literature or formal talks; conversation is more everyday.
entries.definitionCN: 强调两方或多方之间的交流，常用于文学或正式会谈；conversation 更日常。

entries.definition: A light, friendly talk with no serious purpose; conversation can be serious as well as casual.
entries.definitionCN: 没有严肃目的的轻松友好谈话；conversation 既可严肃也可随意。

entries.definition: The broad everyday noun for speaking to someone; conversation adds the idea of exchange and turn-taking.
entries.definitionCN: 指与某人说话的最宽泛日常名词；conversation 多出「交流与轮流发言」的意思。

entries.definition: A talk organized around a topic or decision; conversation need not have an agenda.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕某个主题或决定组织的谈话；conversation 不必有议程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the turning image, the root family, the scale shift and the modern machine sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：转动的意象、同族词、尺度的变化与现代机器义。

normal.en: The root image is turning together: speakers keep turning the talk back to each other.
normal.cn: 词根意象是一起转动：说话人不断把话转回对方。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: the same turning root gives conversion, a change of form.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：同一个「转动」词根也构成表示形式改变的词。

normal.en: Scale ladder: one talk, a group's talks, a nation's conversation.
normal.cn: 尺度阶梯：一次谈话、一群人的会谈、一个国家的公共讨论。

normal.en: Skill use: making conversation is a social ability, not a topic.
normal.cn: 技能用法：寒暄是一种社交能力，而不是一个话题。

normal.en: Machine use: a chatbot keeps a conversation across many turns.
normal.cn: 机器用法：聊天机器人在许多轮次中维持一段对话。

abstract.en: Picture a ball passed back and forth so that neither hand holds it long.
abstract.cn: 想象一只球被来回传递，哪只手都不长时间握着它。

abstract.en: Picture two people turning a single topic over between them like a stone.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人把同一个话题像石头一样在彼此之间翻来翻去。

abstract.en: Picture a whole country talking to itself through many small rooms.
abstract.cn: 想象整个国家通过许多小房间与自己对话。

examples.en: A short conversation at the door solved the misunderstanding.
examples.cn: 门口的一段短谈解开了误会。

examples.en: The two ministers held private conversations before the summit.
examples.cn: 两位部长在峰会前进行了私下会谈。

examples.en: The software stores the whole conversation for later review.
examples.cn: 软件保存整段对话，供以后查看。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一起转」——话在两人之间转来转去 → 交谈、会话

root: 拉丁语 conversatio「亲近、生活方式」，出自 conversari「与人相处」，再上溯 convertere「转向」= 表示「共同」的前缀 + vertere「转动」。vertere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the turning talk from one informal exchange to a counted episode, formal talks, a social skill, a classroom method, written dialogue, a machine exchange and a public debate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿这场来回转动的谈话展开：一次非正式交流、一次可计数的事件、正式会谈、社交技能、课堂方法、书面对话、机器交流与公共辩论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words passed back and forth like a ball that neither side keeps.
core.cn: 核心意象：话语像球一样来回传递，哪一方都不一直握着。

branches.en: TALK AND ONE TALK: the activity and a single bounded episode are the same exchange at two levels.
branches.cn: 交谈与一次交谈：活动与一个有始有终的片段，是同一交流的两个层面。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL TALKS: the exchange is scaled up to representatives and organizations.
branches.cn: 机构会谈：交流被放大到代表与组织层面。

branches.en: SOCIAL SKILL: a person can be good at keeping the exchange alive.
branches.cn: 社交技能：一个人可以擅长让交流持续下去。

branches.en: PRACTICE AND SCRIPT: spoken exchange can be rehearsed in class or written as dialogue.
branches.cn: 练习与脚本：口头交流可以在课堂上练习，也可以写成对话。

branches.en: MACHINE AND SOCIETY: a chatbot takes turns, and many small talks add up to a public debate.
branches.cn: 机器与社会：聊天机器人轮流发言，许多小谈话汇成公共辩论。

intro.en: Conversation is a Latin noun of turning and keeping company, and its parts also build words about changing, talking and familiarity.
intro.cn: conversation 是一个表示「转动与相处」的拉丁名词，其部件还构成与改变、交谈及熟悉有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere 'to turn' and com- 'together' build convertere and conversari; the noun conversatio is the direct source of English conversation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere「转动」与表示「共同」的前缀构成 convertere 与 conversari；名词 conversatio 是英语 conversation 的直接来源。

items.example: The prefix makes the turning a shared action.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使转动成为共同的动作。

items.example: The root supplies the back-and-forth image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供来回转动的意象。

items.example: The verb underlies both conversation and conversion.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时是交谈与改变两个词的底层来源。

items.example: The frequentative marks repeated contact.
items.exampleCN: 这个反复后缀标记反复接触。

items.example: The noun first named company, not talk.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词最初命名相处，而不是谈话。

items.example: One conversation can change a decision.
items.exampleCN: 一次谈话就能改变一个决定。

items.example: The guide uses a conversational tone.
items.exampleCN: 这本指南使用口语化的语气。

items.example: She is conversant with the local rules.
items.exampleCN: 她熟悉当地规则。

items.example: Conversion shares the root but not the talk.
items.exampleCN: 表示形式改变的同族词共享词根，却没有谈话义。

derivatives.meaning: an object or painting that prompts talk
derivatives.meaningCN: 引发谈话的物件或群像画

definition_zh: 交谈的；会话式的；口语化的；便于对话的
definition_en: relating to conversation, or sounding like ordinary talk rather than formal writing
core_image: 文字脱下礼服，换上居家衣服，像在桌边和人说话
scene: 编辑把论文里生硬的句子改成聊天般的口吻，在批注里写道：The report needs a more conversational tone.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「口语化、像日常交谈的」（第 2 个义项：语言风格接近口头交谈）；句意为这份报告需要更口语化的语气。

pos.zh: 交谈的；会话式的；口语化的；便于对话的

senses.title: Relating to conversation
senses.definition: concerned with conversation as an activity or with the way people talk together
senses.definitionCN: 与作为活动的交谈、或与人们一起谈话的方式有关
senses.example: Conversational analysis examines how speakers take turns.
senses.exampleCN: 交谈分析研究说话人如何轮流发言。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun to whatever it describes, so its broadest job is 'of conversation'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词连接到被描述之物，因此最宽的用法就是「与交谈有关的」。

senses.title: Informal in style
senses.definition: written or spoken in a relaxed way that resembles everyday talk
senses.definitionCN: 以接近日常谈话的轻松方式写出或说出
senses.example: The guide is written in a conversational tone.
senses.exampleCN: 这本指南以口语化的语气写成。
senses.why: When writing borrows the ease of talk, it is described by the adjective of talk.
senses.whyCN: 当写作借用谈话的轻松感时，就用「交谈」的形容词来描述它。

senses.title: Fluent in everyday speech
senses.definition: describing a learner's ability to speak a language comfortably in ordinary situations
senses.definitionCN: 描述学习者在日常情境中能自如说一门语言
senses.example: She has conversational Spanish but cannot write it well.
senses.exampleCN: 她的西班牙语会话流利，但写不好。
senses.why: Language teaching separates talk from writing, so the adjective marks the spoken level of ability.
senses.whyCN: 语言教学把谈话与写作分开，因此这个形容词标记口语能力水平。

senses.title: Dialogue-based as a method
senses.definition: organized as an exchange between participants rather than as a lecture
senses.definitionCN: 组织成参与者之间的交流，而不是单向讲授
senses.example: The course uses a conversational method rather than lectures.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课采用对话式方法，而不是讲授。
senses.why: A method can be built out of conversation, so the adjective names the form of instruction.
senses.whyCN: 一种方法可以由交谈构成，因此这个形容词命名教学的形式。

senses.title: Interactive in computing
senses.definition: describing a system that responds in natural language over successive turns
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个用自然语言在连续轮次中作出回应的系统
senses.example: The app offers a conversational interface for support.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用提供对话式界面用于支持服务。
senses.why: Software that takes turns like a person borrows the adjective of human talk.
senses.whyCN: 像人一样轮流回应的软件借用了人类交谈的形容词。

senses.title: Inferential in pragmatics
senses.definition: in pragmatics, describing meaning that a listener infers beyond the literal words
senses.definitionCN: 在语用学中，描述听者在字面词语之外推断出的意义
senses.example: A conversational inference goes beyond the literal sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 交谈推断会超出字面句子。
senses.why: Everyday talk relies on shared assumptions, and linguistics names those assumptions by this adjective.
senses.whyCN: 日常谈话依赖共同预设，语言学用这个形容词命名那些预设。

senses.title: Describing an AI agent
senses.titleCN: 描述人工智能对话体的
senses.definition: describing a software agent designed to hold a natural dialogue with users
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个被设计来与用户进行自然对话的软件代理
senses.example: The conversational agent handles routine requests.
senses.exampleCN: 这个对话式智能体处理日常请求。
senses.why: As agents gained the ability to sustain turns, the adjective became a standard product label.
senses.whyCN: 当智能体获得维持轮次的能力，这个形容词便成为标准的产品标签。

senses.title: Disposed to talk
senses.definition: in a mood for friendly talk; sociable and ready to converse
senses.definitionCN: 有心情进行友好谈话的；合群的、愿意交谈的
senses.example: He was in a conversational mood after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后他很有聊天的兴致。
senses.why: A temporary mood can be named by the same adjective, pointing to the person rather than the language.
senses.whyCN: 暂时的情绪也可以用同一个形容词来命名，这时指向的是人而不是语言。

intro.en: Conversational is an English adjective built from conversation plus the Latin-derived suffix -al. Conversation itself comes from Latin conversatio 'familiar intercourse'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: conversational 是由 conversation 加源自拉丁语的关系形容词后缀构成的英语形容词。conversation 本身来自拉丁语 conversatio「亲近交往」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Conversatio named familiar intercourse or a way of life, from conversari 'to keep company', itself from convertere 'to turn around'.
items.cn: conversatio 指亲近交往或生活方式，出自 conversari「与人相处」，后者又来自 convertere「转向」。

items.en: Old French conversation brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century, where it gradually narrowed toward talk.
items.cn: 古法语 conversation 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，其意义逐渐收窄到谈话。

items.en: By the sixteenth century English conversation centred on the exchange of talk between people.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，英语 conversation 已以人与人之间的谈话交流为核心。

items.en: Conversational is recorded in the eighteenth century, formed with the adjective suffix that marks relation.
items.cn: conversational 在十八世纪见于记录，由标记关系的形容词后缀构成。

items.en: In the twentieth and twenty-first centuries the adjective extended to teaching methods, pragmatics, interfaces and AI agents.
items.cn: 到二十与二十一世纪，这个形容词扩展到教学方法、语用学、界面与人工智能代理。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation of the adjective is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of the turning root remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个形容词确切的最早书证没有定论，表示「转动」的词根在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the noun and morphological relatives of the adjective; group two holds near synonyms for a relaxed spoken style.
note.cn: 第一组是名词及这个形容词的构词亲属；第二组是表示轻松口语风格的近义词。

entries.definition: The noun names the talk itself; the adjective describes anything that resembles or belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词命名谈话本身；形容词描述任何与它相似或属于它的事物。

entries.definition: It names a person who is good at conversation, not a style of language.
entries.definitionCN: 命名善于交谈的人，而不是语言风格。

entries.definition: It means familiar with a subject, from having dealt with it; it does not mean talkative or informal.
entries.definitionCN: 意为熟悉某个主题，来自与之打过交道；并不是「爱说话」或「口语化」的意思。

entries.definition: The verb means to talk with someone, and the noun means the opposite statement; neither carries the style meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 动词意为与人交谈，名词意为相反命题；两者都不带「风格」义。

entries.definition: It describes language suitable for ordinary informal talk; conversational stresses the sound of a real exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 描述适合日常非正式谈话的语言；conversational 强调真实交流的语气。

entries.definition: The broad adjective for anything without ceremony; conversational is narrower and specifically talk-like.
entries.definitionCN: 指不拘礼节的宽泛形容词；conversational 更窄，特指像谈话的。

entries.definition: It describes a light, friendly style or a person who talks a lot; conversational can still be serious.
entries.definitionCN: 形容轻松友好的风格或话多的人；conversational 仍可严肃。

entries.definition: It stresses two-way response, especially in media; conversational adds the natural-language, turn-taking quality.
entries.definitionCN: 强调双向回应，尤其在媒体中；conversational 多出自然语言与轮流发言的特质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the noun base, the style sense and the modern interface sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：名词基础、风格义与现代界面义。

normal.en: The adjective is the noun plus a relation suffix: anything of or like talk.
normal.cn: 这个形容词是名词加关系后缀：任何属于谈话或像谈话的事物。

normal.en: Style use: a conversational tone reads as if the writer is speaking to you.
normal.cn: 风格用法：口语化的语气读起来像作者在对你说话。

normal.en: Language use: conversational Spanish means you can talk, not necessarily write.
normal.cn: 语言用法：会话西班牙语指能说，不一定能写。

normal.en: Technology use: a conversational interface answers in turns.
normal.cn: 技术用法：对话式界面按轮次作答。

normal.en: The opposite is a formal or academic register.
normal.cn: 反面是正式或学术语体。

abstract.en: Picture a textbook taking off its jacket and sitting down at a kitchen table.
abstract.cn: 想象一本教科书脱下外套，在厨房桌边坐下。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that pauses to let you answer.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话会停下来等你回答。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that waits its turn instead of printing a block of text.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器会等轮次，而不是直接打印一大段文字。

examples.en: The manual's conversational style makes the rules easier to remember.
examples.cn: 这本手册口语化的风格让规则更容易记住。

examples.en: After a year abroad, his conversational French became confident.
examples.cn: 在国外待了一年后，他的法语会话变得自信。

examples.en: The team tested a conversational agent with real customers.
examples.cn: 团队用真实客户测试了一个对话式智能体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 交谈加「的」——像聊天一样的 → 口语化的、会话式的

root: 英语 conversation 加源自拉丁语的关系形容词后缀；conversation 来自拉丁语 conversatio「亲近交往」，再上溯 conversari「与人相处」与 convertere「转向」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one adjective to the activity, the style, the learner's fluency, a method, an interface, an inference, an AI agent and a sociable mood.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用于活动、风格、学习者流利度、方法、界面、推断、人工智能代理与合群情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: written or spoken language dressed as a relaxed talk across a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：书面或口头语言穿得像桌边轻松谈话。

branches.en: TALK AND INFERENCE: the study of conversation includes the assumptions listeners draw beyond the words.
branches.cn: 交谈与推断：对交谈的研究包括听者在词语之外作出的预设。

branches.en: STYLE AND MOOD: a talk-like style and a talk-ready mood both lower the barrier to speaking.
branches.cn: 风格与情绪：像谈话的风格与愿意谈话的情绪都降低了开口的门槛。

branches.en: FLUENCY: the ability to hold an everyday spoken exchange.
branches.cn: 流利度：维持日常口头交流的能力。

branches.en: STRUCTURED EXCHANGE: a teaching method and an interface both organize responses as turns.
branches.cn: 结构化交流：教学方法与界面都把回应组织成轮次。

branches.en: AGENT: software that is built to sustain a natural dialogue.
branches.cn: 代理：为维持自然对话而构建的软件。

intro.en: Conversational adds a relation suffix to the noun of talk, and the family around it covers talking, familiarity and machine dialogue.
intro.cn: conversational 在表示谈话的名词上加了关系后缀，它周围的词族涵盖交谈、熟悉与机器对话。

latinIntro.en: Latin conversari 'to keep company' gives conversation and conversant; convertere 'to turn around' supplies the root image; English adds -al, -ly and -ist.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 conversari「与人相处」衍生 conversation 与 conversant；convertere「转向」提供词根意象；英语再加关系、副词与施动者后缀。

items.example: A good conversation can last hours.
items.exampleCN: 一场好的交谈可以持续数小时。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.example: The letter has a conversational warmth.
items.exampleCN: 这封信有一种交谈式的温暖。

items.example: He answered conversationally, without notes.
items.exampleCN: 他像聊天一样回答，没有看稿。

items.example: She is a lively conversationalist.
items.exampleCN: 她是个生动的交谈者。

items.example: He is conversant with the local law.
items.exampleCN: 他熟悉当地法律。

items.meaning: a system that answers in dialogue
items.example: The bank launched a conversational interface.
items.exampleCN: 这家银行推出了对话式界面。

items.example: The conversational agent books appointments.
items.exampleCN: 这个对话式智能体负责预约。

items.meaning: meaning inferred from how something is said
items.meaningCN: 从说话方式推断出的意义
items.example: The pause carried a conversational implicature.
items.exampleCN: 那段停顿带有交谈推断的意义。

definition_zh: 对话；对白；（正式）磋商；对话体作品
definition_en: a conversation between two or more people, especially one that exchanges ideas
core_image: 两束声音穿过中间的空隙，来回碰撞，谁也不压住谁
scene: 两国代表在长桌两侧轮流发言，记者在报道中写道：The dialogue resumed after months of silence.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「双方或多方之间的对话」（第 1 个义项：两人以上交流看法）；句意为沉默数月之后对话重新开始。

pos.zh: 对话；对白；正式磋商；对话体作品
（较少用）进行对话；用对话表达

senses.title: Conversation between two or more people
senses.titleCN: 两人或多人之间的对话
senses.definition: a spoken exchange in which two or more people take turns
senses.definitionCN: 两人或多人轮流发言的口头交流
senses.example: The film's dialogue sounds natural and unforced.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的对白听起来自然、不做作。
senses.why: The Greek root joins 'between' with 'speech', so the word begins as speech that passes between parties.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根把「之间」与「言语」结合，因此这个词一开始就是在各方之间穿行的言语。

senses.title: An exchange of views or negotiation
senses.definition: organized discussion between parties who may disagree, aimed at mutual understanding
senses.definitionCN: 可能存在分歧的各方之间有组织的讨论，旨在相互理解
senses.example: The two sides opened a dialogue on water rights.
senses.exampleCN: 双方就水权开启了对话。
senses.why: When the parties are institutions, the between-ness becomes the point: the talk is a channel between positions.
senses.whyCN: 当各方是机构时，「之间」本身成了重点：谈话是立场之间的通道。

senses.title: A literary form
senses.definition: a work written as a conversation, especially a philosophical or instructive one
senses.definitionCN: 以谈话形式写成的作品，尤其是哲学或教导性的作品
senses.example: Plato wrote philosophy as dialogue.
senses.exampleCN: 柏拉图以对话体写作哲学。
senses.why: The form preserves the back-and-forth of speech instead of flattening it into a single voice.
senses.whyCN: 这种体裁保留言语的来回往复，而不是把它压平成单一声音。

senses.title: Scripted speech in film or theatre
senses.definition: the lines spoken by characters in a script, film or play
senses.definitionCN: 剧本、电影或戏剧中人物说出的台词
senses.example: The dialogue was improvised on set.
senses.exampleCN: 这些对白是在片场即兴的。
senses.why: Performance writes down the between-speech and calls the written version dialogue.
senses.whyCN: 表演把「之间的言语」写下来，并把写成的版本称为对白。

senses.title: A philosophical method
senses.definition: a method of inquiry that proceeds through questions and answers rather than a lecture
senses.definitionCN: 通过问答而不是讲授推进的探究方法
senses.example: Socratic dialogue proceeds by questions rather than assertions.
senses.exampleCN: 苏格拉底式对话靠提问而不是断言推进。
senses.why: Philosophy turned the exchange into a method, where each answer opens the next question.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把这种交流变成方法，每个回答都打开下一个问题。

senses.title: Internal dialogue
senses.definition: the conversation a person holds with themselves in thought
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在思想中与自己的交谈
senses.example: She kept a silent dialogue with herself before the speech.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲前她与自己进行了一场无声的对话。
senses.why: The between-ness can be internal: one mind takes both parts of the exchange.
senses.whyCN: 「之间」可以转向内部：一个心灵承担交流的双方。

senses.title: A dialog box in computing
senses.definition: a small window that asks the user for information or a decision
senses.definitionCN: 向用户索取信息或要求作出决定的小窗口
senses.example: A dialog box asked for the password.
senses.exampleCN: 一个对话框要求输入密码。
senses.why: The interface borrows the word because the box conducts a short exchange with the user.
senses.whyCN: 界面借用这个词，因为这个框与用户进行一段简短交流。

senses.title: Classroom dialogue
senses.definition: collaborative talk among students and teachers used as a tool for learning
senses.definitionCN: 师生之间作为学习工具的合作性谈话
senses.example: Classroom dialogue improves reasoning more than lecturing does.
senses.exampleCN: 课堂对话比讲授更能改善推理。
senses.why: Education treats talk as a way of thinking together, so the exchange becomes a learning method.
senses.whyCN: 教育把谈话当作共同思考的方式，因此交流成为学习方法。

intro.en: Dialogue comes through Latin and French from Greek dialogos, built on dia- 'through, between' and logos 'word, speech, reason'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dialogue 经拉丁语与法语来自希腊语 dialogos，由希腊语表示「穿过、之间」的前缀与 logos「词、言语、理性」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, speech, account, reason'. Its deeper origin is connected with a verb meaning 'to gather or say', but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: logos 意为「词、言语、叙述、理性」。其更深来源与一个表示「收集、说」的动词有关，但重构并不确定。

items.en: Dia- meant 'through, across, between', and in dialogos it marked speech passing between parties.
items.cn: 这个希腊前缀意为「穿过、横过、之间」，在 dialogos 中标记在各方之间穿行的言语。

items.en: Dialogos named a conversation or a philosophical exchange; Plato made it the name of a literary form.
items.cn: dialogos 指谈话或哲学交流；柏拉图使它成为一种文学体裁的名称。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as dialogus and passed it to medieval and modern European languages.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊词成为 dialogus，并把它传给中世纪与现代欧洲语言。

items.en: English dialogue appears in the thirteenth century through French; the American spelling dialog became common in computing.
items.cn: 英语 dialogue 在十三世纪经法语出现；美式拼写 dialog 在计算领域变得常见。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact pre-Greek origin of logos is debated, and the first English citation of the literary sense is not fixed; proposed roots are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：logos 在希腊语之前的来源有争议，文学义的最早英语书证也没有定论；提出的词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the spelling variant and words built with different prefixes from the same speech root; group two holds near synonyms for an exchange of talk.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写变体，以及与同一「言语」词根搭配不同前缀的词；第二组是表示交谈的近义词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the same word, now standard for the computing window and common in US fiction.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的美式拼写，现为计算机窗口的标准写法，也常用于美国小说。

entries.definition: The second part comes from a Greek verb meaning 'to speak' in a different root line; a dialect is a regional variety, not a conversation.
entries.definitionCN: 后半部分来自另一条词根线上表示「说话」的希腊动词；方言是地区变体，不是对话。

entries.definition: A play or scene for exactly two speakers; dialogue has no such numerical limit.
entries.definitionCN: 为恰好两个说话人写的戏剧或场景；dialogue 没有这种人数限制。

entries.definition: It uses a prefix meaning 'one' with the same speech root, so it names a long speech by a single voice.
entries.definitionCN: 用表示「一」的前缀与同一言语词根组合，命名单一声音的长篇发言。

entries.definition: The everyday word for informal talk; dialogue often implies an exchange between sides or a literary form.
entries.definitionCN: 指非正式谈话的日常用词；dialogue 常暗示各方之间的交流或文学形式。

entries.definition: A talk organized around a topic or decision; dialogue stresses the exchange between voices.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕主题或决定组织的谈话；dialogue 强调声音之间的交流。

entries.definition: Formal negotiations between parties; dialogue can be broader and need not aim at a settlement.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的正式谈判；dialogue 可以更宽，也不必以达成协议为目标。

entries.definition: A general word for giving and receiving; dialogue is specifically an exchange of speech.
entries.definitionCN: 指给予与接受的宽泛词；dialogue 特指言语的交换。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the 'between' prefix, the speech root, the literary form and the modern window.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「之间」的前缀、「言语」词根、文学形式与现代窗口。

normal.en: The prefix means 'between', the root means 'speech', so dialogue is speech passing between people.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「之间」，词根意为「言语」，因此对话就是在人与人之间穿行的言语。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: one voice gives a monologue, two voices a duologue, many voices a dialogue.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：一个声音是独白，两个声音是双人对话，多个声音是对话。

normal.en: Plato turned the exchange into a literary form that still bears the name.
normal.cn: 柏拉图把这种交流变成一种至今仍用此名的文学体裁。

normal.en: Film and theatre call the written talk of characters dialogue.
normal.cn: 电影与戏剧把人物写下来的谈话称为对白。

normal.en: Computing uses the shorter American spelling for a dialog box.
normal.cn: 计算领域用较短的美式拼写指对话框。

abstract.en: Picture two voices meeting in the empty space between two chairs.
abstract.cn: 想象两个声音在两张椅子之间的空处相遇。

abstract.en: Picture a question and an answer holding hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问题与一个回答手拉着手。

abstract.en: Picture a small window that asks you one question before it opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小窗口在打开之前先问你一个问题。

examples.en: The novel is mostly dialogue, with very little description.
examples.cn: 这部小说大部分是对白，描写很少。

examples.en: The union and the management agreed to resume dialogue.
examples.cn: 工会与管理层同意恢复对话。

examples.en: A dialogue box appeared asking whether to save the file.
examples.cn: 弹出一个对话框，询问是否保存文件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「两者之间」加「说话」——两边来回说 → 对话、对白

root: 希腊语 dialogos = 表示「穿过、之间」的前缀 + logos「词、言语、理性」，经拉丁语 dialogus 与法语进入英语。logos 的更早来源有争议，相关词根为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow speech between parties: a general exchange, formal talks, a literary form, a script, a philosophical method, inner talk, a computer window and classroom learning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿「各方之间的言语」展开：一般交流、正式磋商、文学体裁、脚本、哲学方法、内心交谈、计算机窗口与课堂学习。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two streams of speech cross the space between two parties.
core.cn: 核心意象：两股言语穿过两方之间的空间。

branches.en: EXCHANGE: ordinary turn-taking and classroom talk both use speech as a shared tool.
branches.cn: 交流：日常轮流发言与课堂谈话都把言语当作共享工具。

branches.en: BETWEEN SIDES: the parties may disagree, and the talk is the channel between their positions.
branches.cn: 各方之间：各方可能存在分歧，谈话是立场之间的通道。

branches.en: FORM AND METHOD: a written dialogue preserves turn-taking, and a philosophical dialogue turns it into inquiry.
branches.cn: 形式与方法：书面对话保留轮流往复，哲学对话把它变成探究。

branches.en: SCRIPT: performance writes the exchange down as lines for characters.
branches.cn: 脚本：表演把交流写成人物的台词。

branches.en: INNER AND MACHINE: one mind can take both parts, and a window can take the other part for a machine.
branches.cn: 内心与机器：一个心灵可以承担双方，一个窗口也可以替机器承担另一方。

intro.en: Dialogue is a Greek compound of 'between' and 'speech', and the same pieces build monologue, duologue and the adjective of dialogic form.
intro.cn: dialogue 是希腊语中「之间」与「言语」的合成词，同样的部件还构成独白、双人对话与对话形式的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Greek dia- and logos formed dialogos, which Latin borrowed as dialogus; English adds adjective and adverb suffixes to build the family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语表示「穿过、之间」的前缀与 logos 构成 dialogos，拉丁语借入为 dialogus；英语再加形容词与副词后缀构成词族。

items.example: The prefix marks speech crossing between parties.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记在各方之间穿行的言语。

items.example: The root names speech and its rational order.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名言语及其理性秩序。

items.example: The Greek word named an exchange of speeches.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词命名言语的交换。

items.example: Latin kept the word for learned conversation.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留这个词指有学问的交谈。

items.example: The class used a dialogical approach.

items.example: The actor delivered a long monologue.
items.exampleCN: 演员说了一段长长的独白。

items.example: The second act is a duologue.
items.exampleCN: 第二幕是一段双人对话。

items.meaning: a regional variety of a language
