items.exampleCN: 这种方言在元音上与标准语不同。

definition_zh: 论点；论证；争论；论据；（数学与编程中的）自变量
definition_en: a set of reasons given to support a belief, or a disagreement between people
core_image: 一列理由排成队，把结论稳稳抬起来
scene: 研讨会上两人围绕同一组数据给出相反结论，主持人提醒说：Their argument turned on how the data were read.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「由理由支撑的论证」（第 1 个义项：用理由支持结论）；句意为他们的论证取决于数据如何解读。

pos.zh: 论点；论证；争论；论据；自变量

senses.title: A reasoned case
senses.definition: a set of reasons offered to support a conclusion or belief
senses.definitionCN: 为支持某个结论或信念而提出的一组理由
senses.example: Her argument rests on three independent studies.
senses.exampleCN: 她的论证建立在三项独立研究之上。
senses.why: The Latin source named evidence or proof, so the core sense is a structure of reasons holding up a claim.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源命名证据或证明，因此核心义是由理由支撑主张的结构。

senses.title: A discussion or debate
senses.definition: an exchange in which people present and test opposing cases
senses.definitionCN: 人们提出并检验对立理由的交流
senses.example: The argument lasted all afternoon without a conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这场辩论持续了整个下午，仍无结论。
senses.why: When two reasoned cases meet, the activity of presenting them becomes the argument itself.
senses.whyCN: 当两套论证相遇时，呈现它们的过程本身就成了这场争论。

senses.title: A quarrel
senses.definition: an angry disagreement in which people speak against each other
senses.definitionCN: 人们互相指责、情绪激烈的分歧
senses.example: They had an argument about money and left separately.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为钱吵了一架，各自离开。
senses.why: The reasoned case can collapse into heat, and the word follows it into the emotional register.
senses.whyCN: 有理由的论证可以塌成火气，这个词也跟着进入情绪层面。

senses.title: Premises leading to a conclusion in logic
senses.titleCN: 逻辑中由前提推出结论
senses.definition: in logic, a structured set of premises intended to establish a conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑中，为确立结论而组织起来的一组前提
senses.example: A valid argument can still have a false premise.
senses.exampleCN: 有效的论证仍可能有错误的前提。
senses.why: Logic formalizes the reasoned case, separating its skeleton from its content.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把有理由的论证形式化，把骨架与内容分开。

senses.title: An independent variable in mathematics
senses.definition: in mathematics and computing, a value passed to a function or operation
senses.definitionCN: 在数学与计算中，传给函数或运算的值
senses.example: The function takes two arguments and returns a list.
senses.exampleCN: 这个函数接收两个自变量并返回一个列表。
senses.why: A function 'argues' from its inputs to its output, so the input acquired the name of what is reasoned from.
senses.whyCN: 函数从输入推到输出，因此输入获得了「被据以推理之物」的名称。

senses.title: A syntactic participant
senses.definition: in linguistics, a phrase that a verb requires in order to complete its meaning
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，动词为完成意义所必需的短语
senses.example: The verb requires two arguments, a subject and an object.
senses.exampleCN: 这个动词需要两个论元，一个主语和一个宾语。
senses.why: Linguistics borrowed the logical idea: a predicate needs certain participants to make a complete proposition.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借用了逻辑观念：一个谓词需要某些参与者才能构成完整命题。

senses.title: A summary or outline
senses.definition: an old literary sense: a short statement of the subject or plot of a work
senses.definitionCN: 一个旧的文学义：对作品主题或情节的简短说明
senses.example: The argument of the play appears in the programme.
senses.exampleCN: 这部剧的情节梗概印在节目单上。
senses.why: A summary sets out the matter to be proved or followed, which is why the word once meant the contents of a work.
senses.whyCN: 提要把要证明或要跟随的内容摆出来，因此这个词曾指作品的内容概要。

senses.title: A legal case presented in words
senses.titleCN: 以言辞陈述的法律主张
senses.definition: a lawyer's reasoned statement of a case before a court
senses.definitionCN: 律师在法庭上对案件作出的有理由陈述
senses.example: Counsel presented the argument in writing before the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 律师在听证前以书面形式提交了论证。
senses.why: Law is one of the oldest homes of formal reasoning, so a pleaded case is called an argument.
senses.whyCN: 法律是形式推理最古老的居所之一，因此被陈述的案件主张被称为论证。

intro.en: Argument comes through Old French from Latin argumentum 'evidence, proof, subject of contention', formed from arguere 'to make clear, prove, accuse'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: argument 经古法语来自拉丁语 argumentum「证据、证明、争点」，由 arguere「使清楚、证明、指控」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arguere meant 'to make clear, prove, accuse'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes proposed to a root meaning 'to shine' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: arguere 意为「使清楚、证明、指控」。其更深来源不确定；有人把它系于某个表示「发亮」的词根，那只是重构。

items.en: Argumentum named evidence, a proof, and also the subject being argued about; the noun carried both the support and the dispute.
items.cn: argumentum 指证据、证明，也指被争论的主题；这个名词同时携带支撑与争执两面。

items.en: Old French argument entered English in the thirteenth century, first in the senses of proof and topic.
items.cn: 古法语 argument 在十三世纪进入英语，最初具有「证明」与「主题」两个意义。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word regularly named a verbal dispute as well as a reasoned case.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词除指有理由的论证外，也常指口头争执。

items.en: Logic made argument a structure of premises; mathematics and computing later used it for the input of a function, and linguistics for a verb's participant.
items.cn: 逻辑学把论证变成前提结构；数学与计算后来用它指函数的输入，语言学用它指动词的参与者。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of arguere is unsettled, and the date of the mathematical sense is not fixed; proposed root forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：arguere 在拉丁语之前的来源未定，数学义的确切年代也没有定论；提出的词根形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from different roots or different suffixes; group two holds near synonyms for reasoning and dispute.
note.cn: 第一组是来自不同词根或带不同后缀的外形相近词；第二组是表示推理与争执的近义词。

entries.definition: It sounds close but comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to increase'; it means to add to something, not to reason about it.
entries.definitionCN: 读音接近，但来自表示「增加」的拉丁动词；意思是增添，而不是推理。

entries.definition: It names the process or art of constructing arguments rather than a single case.
entries.definitionCN: 命名构建论证的过程或技艺，而不是单个论证。

entries.definition: The adjective describes a person or text that tends to argue; it does not name the case itself.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词描述倾向于争论的人或文本；不命名论证本身。

entries.definition: It means open to dispute or able to be supported by argument, not a complete case.
entries.definitionCN: 意为可争议的或可论证的，而不是一个完整论证。

entries.definition: A disagreement or quarrel; argument can also mean a reasoned case, which dispute cannot.
entries.definitionCN: 分歧或争吵；argument 还可指有理由的论证，而 dispute 不能。

entries.definition: A formal contest of arguments before an audience; argument itself need not be public or rule-bound.
entries.definitionCN: 在观众面前进行的正式论证较量；argument 本身不必公开或受规则约束。

entries.definition: The mental process of drawing conclusions; argument is the expressed structure of reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 得出推论的心理过程；argument 是表达出来的理由结构。

entries.definition: The set of facts and reasons supporting one side; argument often includes the reasoning that connects them.
entries.definitionCN: 支持一方的事实与理由；argument 常包括连接它们的推理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the proving root, the reason structure and the technical extensions.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「证明」的词根、理由结构与技术延伸。

normal.en: The root means 'make clear or prove', so an argument is a set of reasons that makes a claim clear.
normal.cn: 词根意为「使清楚、证明」，因此论证就是让主张变清楚的一组理由。

normal.en: Four settings: a paper, a debate, a quarrel and a court.
normal.cn: 四个场景：论文、辩论、争吵与法庭。

normal.en: Logic skeleton: premises on one side, conclusion on the other.
normal.cn: 逻辑骨架：一边是前提，另一边是结论。

normal.en: Math use: a function's argument is the value you feed in.
normal.cn: 数学用法：函数的自变量就是你喂进去的值。

normal.en: Linguistics use: a verb's arguments are the participants it needs.
normal.cn: 语言学用法：动词的论元就是它需要的参与者。

abstract.en: Picture a row of reasons standing under a conclusion like pillars.
abstract.cn: 想象一排理由像柱子一样托住结论。

abstract.en: Picture two people pushing the same stone from opposite sides.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人从相反方向推同一块石头。

abstract.en: Picture a number entering a machine and a answer coming out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数字进入机器，一个答案出来。

examples.en: The paper's central argument is that early exposure shapes later skill.
examples.cn: 这篇论文的核心论点是早期接触塑造后来的技能。

examples.en: Their argument in court depended on one disputed document.
examples.cn: 他们在法庭上的论证取决于一份有争议的文件。

examples.en: The programmer passed the wrong argument to the function.
examples.cn: 程序员把错误的实参传给了函数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「使清楚」——把理由摆清楚 → 论证、论点、争论

root: 拉丁语 argumentum「证据、证明、争点」，出自 arguere「使清楚、证明、指控」；arguere 更深来源不确定，相关词根形式为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one reasoned structure: a case, the debate around it, the quarrel it can become, its logical skeleton, its mathematical input, its linguistic participants, its old summary and its legal form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个有理由的结构展开：论证本身、围绕它的辩论、它可能变成的争吵、它的逻辑骨架、数学输入、语言参与者、旧时的提要义与法律形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of reasons lifting a conclusion off the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排理由把结论从地面抬起来。

branches.en: REASONED CASE: a written case and a pleaded case are the same structure of support in different rooms.
branches.cn: 有理由的主张：书面论证与法庭陈述是同一支撑结构出现在不同场合。

branches.en: DISPUTE: two cases meeting can become a debate, and a debate can collapse into a quarrel.
branches.cn: 争执：两套论证相遇可以成为辩论，辩论也可以塌成争吵。

branches.en: LOGIC: premises and conclusion are the bare skeleton of the case.
branches.cn: 逻辑：前提与结论是论证的赤裸骨架。

branches.en: INPUT AND PARTICIPANT: mathematics and grammar both name what a function or verb needs in order to work.
branches.cn: 输入与参与者：数学与语法都命名函数或动词运作所需的东西。

branches.en: SUMMARY: an old sense sets out the matter of a work before the reader meets it.
branches.cn: 提要：旧义在读者接触作品之前先摆出作品的内容。

intro.en: Argument is a Latin noun of making clear and proving, and its root also builds argue, arguable and the adjective of a quarrelsome style.
intro.cn: argument 是一个表示「使清楚、证明」的拉丁名词，其词根还构成 argue、arguable 以及表示好争风格的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin arguere 'to prove, accuse' gives argumentum; English adds -ment, -able, -ative and -ation to build the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 arguere「证明、指控」衍生 argumentum；英语再加名词、形容词与过程后缀构成词族。

items.example: The root names the act of making a claim clear.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名让主张变清楚的动作。

items.example: The Latin noun carried both proof and dispute.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词同时携带证明与争执。

items.meaning: result or means of an action
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a thing produced.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成所产生之物。

items.example: The argument was clear but incomplete.
items.exampleCN: 这个论证清楚但不完整。

items.example: They argued for a different reading.
items.exampleCN: 他们为另一种解读辩护。

items.example: The claim is arguable but not proven.
items.exampleCN: 这个主张可争辩，但未被证明。

items.example: It is arguably the best solution.
items.exampleCN: 可以说这是最好的方案。

items.example: The course teaches argumentation.
items.exampleCN: 这门课教授论证方法。

items.example: The essay takes an argumentative form.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章采用论证性形式。

items.example: The similar sound hides a different root.
items.exampleCN: 相似的读音掩盖了不同的词根。

definition_zh: 爱争论的；论证性的；说理式的
definition_en: tending to argue or disagree, or concerned with presenting reasoned argument
core_image: 一个人手里举着一列理由，随时准备把对方的话推回去
scene: 写作课上老师要求把观点写成有理由支撑的文章，提醒道：This assignment calls for an argumentative essay.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「以论证方式展开的」（第 3 个义项：写作或言谈以理由支撑主张）；句意为这项作业要求写一篇议论文。

pos.zh: 爱争论的；论证性的；说理式的

derivatives.zh: 好争辩地；以论证方式地

senses.title: Fond of arguing
senses.definition: having a habit of disagreeing and arguing with others, often in a quarrelsome way
senses.definitionCN: 有与他人分歧争吵的习惯，常带好斗意味
senses.example: He gets argumentative when he is tired.
senses.exampleCN: 他累的时候就会变得爱争论。
senses.why: The suffix marks a tendency, and the base is the activity of arguing, so the word describes a person inclined to it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀标记倾向，词基是争论这一活动，因此这个词描述倾向于它的个人。

senses.title: Eager to test claims by argument
senses.titleCN: 热衷于用论证检验主张的
senses.definition: ready to challenge and examine ideas through reasoned exchange
senses.definitionCN: 愿意通过有理由的交流来质疑与检验观点
senses.example: She is argumentative in the best sense: she tests every claim.
senses.exampleCN: 她是最好的那种好辩：每个主张都要检验。
senses.why: The same tendency can be valued rather than blamed when the arguing is disciplined by reasons.
senses.whyCN: 当争论受理由约束时，同一种倾向可以被肯定而不是被责备。

senses.title: Presenting reasons in writing or speech
senses.titleCN: 在写作或言谈中提出理由的
senses.definition: of a text or speech, organized to support a position with reasons
senses.definitionCN: 指文本或演讲，组织起来用理由支持某个立场
senses.example: The assignment is an argumentative essay, not a report.
senses.exampleCN: 这项作业是议论文，不是报告。
senses.why: A genre can be named by its dominant activity, so a text built from arguments is argumentative.
senses.whyCN: 一种体裁可以按其主导活动命名，因此由论证构成的文本就是论证性的。

senses.title: Persuasive in purpose
senses.definition: designed to persuade an audience by appealing to reasons and values
senses.definitionCN: 通过诉诸理由与价值来试图说服受众
senses.example: Her argumentative strategy appealed to shared values.
senses.exampleCN: 她的说服策略诉诸共同价值。
senses.why: Argument aims at assent, so a text that argues is also a text that tries to move the reader.
senses.whyCN: 论证以获致认同为目标，因此进行论证的文本也是试图打动读者的文本。

senses.title: Concerning the structure of arguments
senses.definition: in logic and rhetoric, relating to the form and validity of arguments
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑与修辞学中，与论证的形式和有效性有关
senses.example: The course covers argumentative validity and fallacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课讲授论证的有效性与谬误。
senses.why: A discipline can study the object named by the base, so the adjective labels work about arguments themselves.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科可以研究词基所命名的对象，因此这个形容词标记关于论证本身的工作。

senses.title: Contested in legal style
senses.titleCN: 法律文书中带争辩性的
senses.definition: of a legal document, setting out a contested position rather than merely recording facts
senses.definitionCN: 指法律文书陈述有争议的立场，而不只是记录事实
senses.example: The brief is argumentative rather than neutral.
senses.exampleCN: 这份书状是争辩性的，而不是中立的。
senses.why: Law separates neutral records from documents that press a case, and the adjective marks the latter.
senses.whyCN: 法律把中立记录与推动主张的文书分开，这个形容词标记后者。

senses.title: Combative in tone
senses.definition: carrying a tone of challenge or confrontation in discussion
senses.definitionCN: 在讨论中带有挑战或对抗的语气
senses.example: The meeting grew argumentative after the budget was raised.
senses.exampleCN: 预算被提出后，会议变得火药味十足。
senses.why: Tone is the emotional colour of an exchange, and a quarrelsome colour makes the exchange argumentative.
senses.whyCN: 语气是交流的情绪色彩，好争的色彩使交流变得火药味十足。

senses.title: Open to dispute as a topic
senses.definition: describing a question or issue on which reasonable people can disagree
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个通情达理的人也可能有分歧的问题或议题
senses.example: Whether the policy helped remains an argumentative question.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策是否有帮助仍是一个可争辩的问题。
senses.why: Some questions invite argument rather than settle it, and the adjective names that openness.
senses.whyCN: 有些问题招来论证而不是被解决，这个形容词命名的正是这种开放性。

intro.en: Argumentative is formed from argument plus the Latin-derived suffix -ative, which marks a tendency. Argument itself comes from Latin argumentum 'proof'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: argumentative 由 argument 加源自拉丁语、标记倾向的后缀构成。argument 本身来自拉丁语 argumentum「证明」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arguere meant 'to make clear, prove, accuse'; its pre-Latin origin is uncertain, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: arguere 意为「使清楚、证明、指控」；其在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，常为它提出的词根是重构。

items.en: Argumentum named proof, evidence and the matter under dispute, and passed through French into English.
items.cn: argumentum 指证明、证据与争议事项，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ativus formed adjectives of tendency or function, saying what something is inclined to do.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词后缀构成表示倾向或功能的形容词，说明某物倾向于做什么。

items.en: English argumentative is recorded in the seventeenth century, first describing a person given to arguing.
items.cn: 英语 argumentative 在十七世纪见于记录，最初描述爱争论的人。

items.en: Later it became a standard label for a kind of essay or speech that presents reasons for a position.
items.cn: 后来它成为标准标签，指一种提出理由支持立场的文章或演讲。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of arguere remains unsettled; proposed root forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：确切的最早书证没有定论，arguere 在拉丁语之前的来源也未确定；提出的词根形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes built with different roots or different suffixes; group two holds near synonyms for a quarrelsome or persuasive manner.
note.cn: 第一组是用不同词根或不同后缀构成的外形相近词；第二组是表示好争或说服态度的近义词。

entries.definition: It looks parallel but comes from a verb meaning 'to increase', so it means adding or enlarging, not arguing.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来结构平行，但来自表示「增加」的动词，因此意思是增添或扩大，不是争论。

entries.definition: It comes from a word for a source of power or expertise and means commanding trust, not fond of argument.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示权力或专业来源的词，意为有权威的，而不是爱争论的。

entries.definition: It names the process of building arguments; the adjective describes a person or text characterized by that process.
entries.definitionCN: 命名构建论证的过程；这个形容词描述以该过程为特征的人或文本。

entries.definition: The noun names the case or the dispute itself, while the adjective describes the tendency or the genre.
entries.definitionCN: 名词命名论证或争论本身，而形容词描述倾向或体裁。

entries.definition: It stresses readiness for conflict; argumentative can be intellectual and need not be hostile.
entries.definitionCN: 强调准备冲突；argumentative 可以是智识性的，不必敌对。

entries.definition: It describes an issue that causes disagreement or a person who likes it; argumentative focuses on the act of arguing.
entries.definitionCN: 描述引起分歧的议题或喜欢分歧的人；argumentative 聚焦于争论行为。

entries.definition: It means inclined to pick quarrels; argumentative can carry no moral blame at all.
entries.definitionCN: 意为动辄找茬争吵；argumentative 可以完全不含道德责备。

entries.definition: It describes the power to move an audience; an argumentative text aims at this but may fail.
entries.definitionCN: 描述打动受众的力量；论证性文本以此为目标，但可能失败。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the tendency suffix, the two faces of arguing and the academic genre.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示倾向的后缀、争论的两副面孔与学术体裁。

normal.en: The suffix means 'tending to', so the word means tending to argue.
normal.cn: 后缀意为「倾向于」，因此这个词意为倾向于争论。

normal.en: Two faces: quarrelsome at the dinner table, reasoned in the seminar room.
normal.cn: 两副面孔：餐桌上好吵，研讨室里讲理。

normal.en: Academic use: an argumentative essay takes a side and defends it with reasons.
normal.cn: 学术用法：议论文选一边，并用理由为之辩护。

normal.en: Law use: an argumentative brief presses a case rather than recording facts.
normal.cn: 法律用法：争辩性书状推动主张，而不是记录事实。

normal.en: The look-alike with a different root means 'increasing', not 'arguing'.
normal.cn: 外形相近而词根不同的那个词意为「增加的」，而不是「争论的」。

abstract.en: Picture a person carrying a stack of reasons like a shield.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把一叠理由像盾牌一样举在身前。

abstract.en: Picture a dinner table that turns into a debating chamber.
abstract.cn: 想象一张餐桌变成辩论场。

abstract.en: Picture an essay with a spine made of because-sentences.
abstract.cn: 想象一篇文章的脊梁由一串「因为」句构成。

examples.en: The tutor asked for an argumentative thesis, not a list of facts.
examples.cn: 导师要求一个有论证的论点，而不是一串事实。

examples.en: He became argumentative whenever the topic turned to money.
examples.cn: 每当话题转到钱，他就变得爱争论。

examples.en: The question is genuinely argumentative, with strong cases on both sides.
examples.cn: 这个问题确实可争辩，双方都有有力论证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 论证加「倾向」——一开口就要论个明白 → 爱争论的、论证性的

root: 英语 argument 加源自拉丁语、表示倾向的后缀；argument 来自拉丁语 argumentum「证明」，再上溯 arguere「使清楚、证明、指控」。arguere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one tendency to a temper, a disciplined habit, a writing genre, a persuasive aim, a logical study, a legal style, a tone and an open question.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一种倾向用于脾气、受约束的习惯、写作文体、说服目的、逻辑研究、法律风格、语气与开放问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person holding a stack of reasons, ready to push back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人举着一叠理由，随时准备推回去。

branches.en: TEMPER AND TONE: a quarrelsome habit and a combative tone are the hot face of the same tendency.
branches.cn: 脾气与语气：好吵的习惯与好斗的语气，是同一倾向的热面孔。

branches.en: DISCIPLINED HABIT: the same readiness can be turned toward testing claims rather than winning.
branches.cn: 受约束的习惯：同一种准备可以转向检验主张，而不是争胜。

branches.en: GENRE AND OPEN QUESTION: an essay built from reasons and an issue that invites reasons share the structure of argument.
branches.cn: 文体与开放问题：由理由构建的文章与招来理由的议题共享论证结构。

branches.en: PERSUASION: argument aims to move an audience toward assent.
branches.cn: 说服：论证旨在把受众推向认同。

branches.en: FORMAL STUDY AND LAW: logic studies the structure, and law presses a contested position.
branches.cn: 形式研究与法律：逻辑研究结构，法律推动有争议的立场。

intro.en: Argumentative joins the argument noun to a suffix of tendency, and the family ranges from the verb argue to the process noun argumentation.
intro.cn: argumentative 把 argument 这一名词接到表示倾向的后缀上，词族从动词 argue 延伸到过程名词 argumentation。

latinIntro.en: Latin argumentum and the suffix -ativus form the adjective; the deeper root arguere means 'to make clear, prove, accuse'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 argumentum 与形容词后缀构成这个形容词；更深的词根 arguere 意为「使清楚、证明、指控」。

items.example: The argument needs a clearer conclusion.
items.exampleCN: 这个论证需要更清楚的结论。

items.example: The suffix marks a habitual direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记习惯性的方向。

items.example: The debate became argumentative.
items.exampleCN: 辩论变得火药味十足。

items.example: He answered argumentatively.
items.exampleCN: 他带着争辩的口气回答。

items.example: Her argumentativeness hid a careful mind.
items.exampleCN: 她的好争辩掩盖了一颗细致的头脑。

items.example: Argumentation is a teachable skill.
items.exampleCN: 论证是一种可教的技能。

items.example: They argued the point for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 他们就这一点争论了一小时。

items.example: The look-alike suffix hides a different root.
items.exampleCN: 这个外形相似的后缀掩盖了不同词根。

definition_zh: 劝说；说服；信念；信念派别；说服力
definition_en: the act of persuading someone, or a belief that someone holds
core_image: 一个人把另一个人心里的方向轻轻扳过来
scene: 销售员没有硬推产品，而是先听客户讲完顾虑，经理评价说：Her persuasion came from listening, not pressure.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「说服、劝说的过程」（第 1 个义项：通过理由或请求使人改变想法）；句意为她的说服力来自倾听，而不是施压。

pos.zh: 劝说；说服；信念；信念派别；说服力

senses.title: The act of persuading
senses.definition: the act of causing someone to believe or do something through reasons or appeals
senses.definitionCN: 通过理由或请求使某人相信或做某事的行为
senses.example: Persuasion works better with reasons than with threats.
senses.exampleCN: 用理由劝说比用威胁更有效。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to urge thoroughly, and the noun names that action of turning a mind toward assent.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「彻底劝」，这个名词命名把心思转向认同的动作。

senses.title: The power to persuade
senses.definition: the quality or force that makes someone able to change another's mind
senses.definitionCN: 使某人能够改变他人想法的性质或力量
senses.example: The speech had a quiet persuasion that no shout could match.
senses.exampleCN: 那场演讲有一种安静的说服力，任何喊叫都比不上。
senses.why: An action can also be viewed as a capacity, so the noun names the force behind successful urging.
senses.whyCN: 一种行为也可以被看作一种能力，因此这个名词命名成功劝说背后的力量。

senses.title: The state of being convinced
senses.definition: the condition of having come to accept something as true or right
senses.definitionCN: 已经接受某事为真或为对的状态
senses.example: After months of argument, the belief settled into persuasion.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数月论证，那个看法沉淀为确信。
senses.why: The action leaves a result behind, and the noun can name the settled state of the changed mind.
senses.whyCN: 行为会留下结果，这个名词可以命名被改变的心思稳定下来的状态。

senses.title: A belief or conviction
senses.definition: a belief held firmly, especially about politics or religion
senses.definitionCN: 坚定持有的信念，尤其关于政治或宗教
senses.example: His political persuasion is a private matter.
senses.exampleCN: 他的政治信念是私事。
senses.why: What one has been persuaded of becomes a possession, so the noun names the content of the conviction.
senses.whyCN: 一个人被说服相信的内容会成为其所有物，因此这个名词命名确信的内容。

senses.title: A group sharing a belief
senses.definition: a body of people who share a particular faith or set of opinions
senses.definitionCN: 共享某种信仰或一套观点的一群人
senses.example: People of every persuasion attended the service.
senses.exampleCN: 持各种信念的人都参加了这场仪式。
senses.why: A belief can mark a community, so the noun extends from the conviction to the people who hold it.
senses.whyCN: 一种信念可以标记一个群体，因此这个名词从确信扩展到持有它的人。

senses.title: The rhetorical art of persuasion
senses.definition: the studied art of moving an audience through speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 通过演讲或写作打动受众的专门技艺
senses.example: Ancient teachers made persuasion a formal subject.
senses.exampleCN: 古代教师把说服变成一门正式学科。
senses.why: Once the action is studied and taught, it becomes an art with rules and techniques.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种行为被研究并教授，它就成为有规则与技巧的技艺。

senses.title: Psychological influence
senses.definition: the process studied by psychology through which attitudes and behaviours are changed
senses.definitionCN: 心理学研究的态度与行为被改变的过程
senses.example: Persuasion research studies how attitudes shift over time.
senses.exampleCN: 说服研究考察态度如何随时间改变。
senses.why: Modern psychology treats the act as a measurable process, so the noun becomes a research object.
senses.whyCN: 现代心理学把这一行为当作可测量的过程，因此这个名词成为研究对象。

senses.title: Diplomatic coaxing
senses.definition: patient urging used in diplomacy to avoid conflict or secure agreement
senses.definitionCN: 外交中为避免冲突或取得协议而进行的耐心劝说
senses.example: The envoy's persuasion avoided a strike.
senses.exampleCN: 特使的劝说避免了一场罢工。
senses.why: In diplomacy the act is slow and repeated, and the noun names that patient pressure.
senses.whyCN: 在外交中，这种行为缓慢而反复，这个名词命名那种耐心的推动。

intro.en: Persuasion comes through Old French from Latin persuasio, from persuadere 'to urge, persuade', built on per- 'thoroughly' and suadere 'to advise, urge'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: persuasion 经古法语来自拉丁语 persuasio，出自 persuadere「力劝、说服」，由表示「彻底」的前缀与 suadere「劝告、敦促」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Suadere meant 'to advise, urge'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; a suggested link to a root meaning 'sweet, pleasant' is a reconstruction, not a proof.
items.cn: suadere 意为「劝告、敦促」。其更深来源不确定；有人把它系于表示「甜、宜人」的词根，那只是重构，并非证明。

items.en: Per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere gave persuadere 'to urge thoroughly, talk someone into something'.
items.cn: 表示「彻底」的前缀加 suadere 构成 persuadere「彻底劝、把某人劝到某事上」。

items.en: The noun persuasio named the act of persuading and also the conviction that resulted from it.
items.cn: 名词 persuasio 既命名劝说的行为，也命名由此产生的确信。

items.en: Old French persuasion entered English in the fourteenth century with both the act and the belief senses.
items.cn: 古法语 persuasion 在十四世纪进入英语，同时带有行为义与信念义。

items.en: By the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the word named a settled conviction and then a community sharing it, especially in religion and politics.
items.cn: 到十六与十七世纪，这个词指稳定的确信，随后指共享它的群体，尤其在宗教与政治领域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of suadere is unsettled, and the date when the group sense became common is not fixed; proposed roots are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：suadere 在拉丁语之前的来源未确定，群体义普及的确切年代也没有定论；提出的词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same urging root or from different roots; group two holds near synonyms for influence and belief.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「敦促」词根或来自不同词根的外形相近词；第二组是表示影响与信念的近义词。

entries.definition: It uses a prefix meaning 'away' with the same urging root, so it names the act of urging someone not to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 用表示「离开」的前缀与同一敦促词根组合，命名劝某人不要做某事的行为。

entries.definition: It shares the 'thoroughly' prefix but its root means 'to turn'; it names a distortion, not an act of urging.
entries.definitionCN: 共享「彻底」前缀，但词根意为「转动」；命名扭曲，而不是劝说行为。

entries.definition: It also shares the prefix, but its root means 'to send or let'; it names consent, not persuasion.
entries.definitionCN: 同样共享前缀，但词根意为「送、允许」；命名许可，而不是说服。

entries.definition: The adjective describes something that has the power to persuade; the noun names the act, force or resulting belief.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词描述有说服力的东西；名词命名行为、力量或由此产生的信念。

entries.definition: A general word for affecting someone or something; persuasion specifically works through reasons or appeals to assent.
entries.definitionCN: 指影响某人或某物的宽泛词；persuasion 特指通过理由或请求促使人认同。

entries.definition: Patient, gentle urging, often repeated; persuasion can be reasoned and need not be gentle.
entries.definitionCN: 耐心温和、常常反复的劝说；persuasion 可以讲理，也不必温和。

entries.definition: A firmly held belief; persuasion can also mean the act or power that produced it.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定持有的信念；persuasion 还可指产生它的行为或力量。

entries.definition: The general state of accepting something as true; persuasion often adds a public or group dimension.
entries.definitionCN: 接受某事为真的宽泛状态；persuasion 常多出公开或群体维度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the urging root, the two results of persuasion and the modern research sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「敦促」的词根、说服的两种结果与现代研究义。

normal.en: The root means 'urge', and the prefix means 'thoroughly', so persuasion is thorough urging.
normal.cn: 词根意为「敦促」，前缀意为「彻底」，因此说服就是彻底的劝说。

normal.en: Two results: a changed mind and a settled belief.
normal.cn: 两个结果：改变的心思与稳定下来的信念。

normal.en: Group use: people of one persuasion share a faith or a politics.
normal.cn: 群体用法：持同一信念的人共享一种信仰或政治立场。

normal.en: Research use: psychology measures how attitudes move under persuasion.
normal.cn: 研究用法：心理学测量态度在说服下如何移动。

normal.en: Contrast pair: persuasion urges toward something, dissuasion urges away from it.
normal.cn: 对比配对：说服把人劝向某事，劝阻把人劝离某事。

abstract.en: Picture a hand gently turning a compass needle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻轻转动指南针的指针。

abstract.en: Picture a locked door opened by a key made of reasons.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇锁着的门被一把由理由做成的钥匙打开。

abstract.en: Picture two people on opposite banks and a bridge built word by word.
abstract.cn: 想象两人各在一岸，一座桥被一个词一个词地搭起来。

examples.en: The campaign relied on persuasion rather than regulation.
examples.cn: 这场运动依靠说服而不是管制。

examples.en: People of different persuasions joined the same committee.
examples.cn: 持不同信念的人加入了同一个委员会。

examples.en: Her quiet persuasion changed the vote at the last minute.
examples.cn: 她安静的说服力在最后一刻改变了投票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「彻底劝」——把对方说动 → 说服、劝说

root: 拉丁语 persuasio，出自 persuadere「力劝、说服」= 表示「彻底」的前缀 + suadere「劝告、敦促」。suadere 更深来源不确定，相关词根形式为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one urging: the act, the power behind it, the convinced state, the belief, the group, the rhetorical art, the psychological process and diplomatic coaxing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次劝说展开：行为本身、背后的力量、被说服的状态、信念、群体、修辞技艺、心理过程与外交斡旋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mind's direction is gently turned toward a new point.
core.cn: 核心意象：心思的方向被轻轻转向一个新的点。

branches.en: URGING: everyday persuasion and slow diplomatic coaxing are the same act at different speeds.
branches.cn: 劝说：日常说服与缓慢的外交斡旋是同一行为的不同速度。

branches.en: POWER: the act can be viewed as a capacity that some speakers or texts possess.
branches.cn: 力量：这种行为可以被看作某些说话人或文本所具有的能力。

branches.en: BELIEF: a changed mind settles into a convinced state and then into a named conviction.
branches.cn: 信念：被改变的心思稳定为确信状态，再成为可命名的信念。

branches.en: GROUP: a shared conviction marks a community of the same persuasion.
branches.cn: 群体：共享的确信标记一个持同一信念的群体。

branches.en: ART AND SCIENCE: rhetoric studies the technique, and psychology studies the process.
branches.cn: 技艺与科学：修辞学研究技巧，心理学研究过程。

intro.en: Persuasion is a Latin noun of thorough urging, and the same root builds persuade, dissuade and the adjectives of persuasive force.
intro.cn: persuasion 是一个表示「彻底敦促」的拉丁名词，同一词根还构成 persuade、dissuade 以及表示说服力的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin per- 'thoroughly' and suadere 'to urge' form persuadere and persuasio; the opposite prefix dis- forms dissuadere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「彻底」的前缀与 suadere「敦促」构成 persuadere 与 persuasio；表示相反方向的前缀构成 dissuadere。

items.example: The prefix strengthens the urging.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加强劝说的力度。

items.example: The root names the act of urging.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名敦促的行为。

items.example: The verb is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成行为名词。

items.meaning: the act of persuading; a belief
items.example: Persuasion changed the room's mood.
items.exampleCN: 说服改变了房间里的气氛。

items.example: She persuaded him to wait.
items.exampleCN: 她劝他等一等。

items.example: The report makes a persuasive case.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告提出了有说服力的论证。

items.example: He argued persuasively for the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他为这个计划作了有说服力的论证。

items.meaning: to urge someone not to do something
items.example: They dissuaded him from resigning.
items.exampleCN: 他们劝他不要辞职。

items.example: Dissuasion is the mirror of persuasion.
items.exampleCN: 劝阻是说服的镜像。
